title: LEAP: Training Logs and Checkpoints for the 95-Run Experiment Matrix (ChinaXiv 202608.00173)
abstract: This dataset contains the complete experimental records for the paper"LEAP: Lagrangian Dual-Ascent Safety Constraints for Latent-Space ModelPredictive Control" (ChinaXiv: 202608.00173,https://chinaxiv.org/abs/202608.00173).Archive: leap95_logs.tar.gz (~2.6 GB). Contents:- logs/{task}/{seed}/{exp}/ Training output of all 95 runs (4 tasks: cheetah-run, quadruped-walk, pendulum-swingup, walker-walk; up to 10 arms; 5 seeds each). Each run directory contains eval.csv (21 evaluation points over 100k steps), models/final.pt (final checkpoint), and eval_video/ (evaluation episode videos).- run_logs/{exp}.log Console logs of every run, including train/eval lines, the four [LEAP-EVAL] violation fields, and Lagrangian dual-variable (lambda) update trajectories; plus driver95.log (acceptance summary of all runs).- action_stats/ Deployment-measurement CSVs (400 episodes), source of Table 2.- analysis_out/ Learning-stage figures and tables, source of Tables 1 and 4.- stats_out/ Statistical test battery outputs (Welch t, paired t, Levene, Holm, etc.).- paper_assets/ Manuscript figures and lambda trajectory tables.- outputs/ Hydra runtime logs (training timeline).Provenance: every number in the paper can be reproduced from this archive.run_logs/*.log -> analyze95.py -> analysis_out/tables/final_performance.csv(Tables 1 and 4); models/final.pt -> collect_action_stats.py ->action_stats/action_stats_summary.csv (Table 2).All standard deviations are population standard deviations over 5 seeds (ddof=0).Code: https://github.com/ylu-lz/leap (analysis scripts:analyze95.py, stats_battery.py, collect_action_stats.py, make_paper_assets.py)

title: Morphological Hijacking in Frozen Language Models: A Contrastive, Symmetry-Regularized Projection Head for Algebraic Structure Recovery
abstract: Preprint, v3. Not yet peer-reviewed. Frozen autoregressive language models cluster surface-similar tokenstogether even when a stronger, task-relevant structure is available inthe input. This paper documents "morphological hijacking" — near-totalcollapse of algebraic-structure recovery under adversarial surfacecorrelation — across four frozen model families (GPT2-small, Pythia-410m,Mistral-7B-v0.3, Qwen2.5-7B), traces it to representational anisotropy,and introduces a lightweight, trainable projection head (contrastiveobjective + positional-symmetry penalty + rogue-dimension ablation +Soft-PCA initialization) that substantially recovers the structure. Theresult is validated at both the discrete-clustering level (Adjusted RandIndex) and the continuous embedding-geometry level (margin, win rate)across five architecturally diverse models, and further tested onnatural English words, a freshly generated 10x-larger constructedlexicon, and (v2) a dedicated test of true algebraic group-positionrecovery with a shuffled-label control. New in v3: a full pre-registered diagnostic pilot testing whether thesame remediation strategy recovers true algebraic COMPOSITION (not justcategory/position classification) — i.e., whether z_i + z_j can berecovered from two independent operand representations. This pilotdocuments a complete, honestly-reported negative result: after rulingout optimization failure, numerical ill-conditioning, and geometricmisalignment between operand representations in turn, and afterconfirming a capacity-controlled MLP fits seen pairs almost perfectly,the same MLP fails to generalize to unseen ordered pairs, falling belowboth a shuffled-label and a wrong-operation control — a cleanmemorization signature, not evidence of learned composition. This resultprecisely delineates what the paper's remediation strategy does and doesnot demonstrate about frozen language models' algebraic structure. Several negative results are reported throughout, including a rejected"globally architectural anisotropy" hypothesis and a rejectedlayer-selection heuristic. This is a preliminary, honestly-scopedempirical report, not a claim of general applicability. Limitations, afull pre-submission checklist, and complete reproducibility code(including the composition-pilot diagnostic chain) are included. Author: Reza NirouyarORCID: 0009-0000-4690-6842Contact: contact@varzin.orgProject website: https://varzin.org

title: Title: Algorithmic Quantum Simulation of Biological Metastasis via Spatio-Temporal Topology
abstract: This paper explores the potential of algorithmic quantum simulation to model the evolution of biological metastasis through the intricate interplay of spatial topology. Traditional simulations struggle to adequately capture the complex, dynamic nature of this phenomenon, particularly the subtle shifts in network structure that drive the process. We propose a novel quantum map approach to represent biological systems, leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to simulate the propagation of microorganisms. The core mechanism focuses on modeling the progression of spatial topology – the arrangement of nodes and connections – as it evolves across time, providing a fundamentally new framework for understanding metastasis. This research investigates the feasibility of simulating key stages of metastasis, including initial contact, clonal expansion, and the formation of metastatic colonies, utilizing quantum-enhanced computational tools. The proposed method promises a significant advancement in our comprehension of biological systems, offering a pathway to more accurate and insightful simulations of complex biological processes.

title: 基于自适应的概率场论的量子算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm based on an adaptive probability field theory (APFT) that automatically adjusts quantum particle parameters to optimize quantum computation performance and enhance the efficiency of quantum algorithms. Traditional quantum algorithms often require manual parameter tuning, which is a time-consuming and error-prone process. Our proposed algorithm leverages adaptive parameter adjustment driven by quantum algorithm optimization to achieve significant performance improvements and stability in quantum computations. The core mechanism involves a dynamic adjustment of the quantum state, guided by a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the algorithm's progress and adjusts parameters to maintain optimal performance. This approach offers a substantial improvement over existing methods, potentially unlocking new capabilities in quantum computation.

title: The title: Topological Topology and the Association of Natural Language Information
abstract: This paper investigates the intriguing intersection of topology and natural language information, proposing a novel approach to enhance the accuracy of natural language understanding. The inherent structure of topological spaces provides a powerful framework for representing and analyzing language's complexities. We explore the potential of leveraging topological structures as a latent feature within natural language data, aiming to create a robust and adaptable model for semantic interpretation. The core of this work lies in the development of a model that dynamically infers the underlying topological properties of language, enabling a deeper and more nuanced understanding of meaning. This research contributes to a paradigm shift in natural language processing, moving beyond traditional statistical methods towards a more holistic and geometrically-informed approach to language representation. Specifically, we construct a model that maps linguistic expressions to topological spaces, enabling the identification of underlying relationships and patterns within the language's structure. The resulting model exhibits improved performance in tasks requiring semantic reasoning and contextual interpretation, demonstrating the significant potential of integrating topological analysis into the field of natural language understanding. This work represents a crucial step towards creating more intelligent and contextually aware language processing systems.

title: 基于量子自适应拓扑的机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm, termed Quantum Adaptive Topology-Based Learning (QATL), leveraging the principles of quantum self-adapted topology to enhance learning capabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QATL through the successful application to a range of complex pattern recognition tasks. The algorithm's core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting a topological structure to capture intricate relationships within the data, leading to improved predictive accuracy and decision-making. The study explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of traditional machine learning techniques, particularly in situations involving high dimensionality and complex non-linear correlations. We analyze the algorithm's strengths and weaknesses, highlighting key design choices and potential avenues for future research. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for various applications, including anomaly detection and data compression.

title: Dynamic Program Abstraction Semantic Consistency Verification (DPSCV)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Program Abstraction Semantic Consistency Verification (DPSCV), a novel approach to ensuring the correctness of dynamic program abstraction. Dynamic program abstraction is a powerful technique for simplifying complex programs, but its success hinges on maintaining semantic consistency across abstraction levels. Traditional static analysis techniques often fail to capture the dynamic nature of abstraction, leading to potential semantic errors. DPSCV addresses this limitation by formally verifying the consistency of abstraction hierarchies using a model checking framework. The core idea is to represent each abstraction level as a state in a state space, enabling systematic verification of the relationships between levels. This paper details the methodology, outlining the key components of the DPSCV framework and illustrating its application with a concrete example. The central claim of DPSCV is that rigorous verification of semantic consistency is paramount for the reliable application of dynamic program abstraction. The core mechanism is a model-checking based approach, providing a systematic method for ensuring the accuracy of the abstraction process.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Topological Field Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic self-adaptive topological field theory, leveraging quantum entanglement to enable instantaneous adjustment of computational topology and achieve unprecedented levels of parallel computation. We propose a new concept, the "Quantum Entanglement Topological" (QET) framework, which utilizes quantum entanglement to dynamically modify the topology of a field, optimizing it in real-time. This approach overcomes limitations of existing topological field theories, offering a fundamentally new computational paradigm. We demonstrate the theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental results supporting this approach, highlighting its potential for transformative advancements in parallel computing.

title: Developing a Transparent Verification Mechanism for Digital Certificates Issued by OpenXPKI using a Merkle Tree
abstract: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) has traditionally relied on centralized Certificate Authorities (CAs), and this architecture introduces a critical single point of failure; a compromised CA can issue fraudulent certificates without immediate detection. In this context, traditional validation protocols, such as CRLs and OCSP, operate reactively post-issuance and fail to architecturally prevent unauthorized generation. This research addresses this architectural gap by designing and implementing a Certificate Transparency (CT) mechanism that is managed locally within an OpenXPKI enterprise environment. This architecture enables independent cryptographic verification of certificate issuance operations while keeping sensitive internal network data isolated from public registries. The proposed system strictly enforces pre-issuance logging by modifying the OpenXPKI workflow to generate a preliminary certificate prior to the final issuance of an X.509 certificate. This preliminary certificate is registered on a standalone server (CT Log) based on a Merkle Tree structure. Following registration, the server issues a Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT) that is directly embedded in the final certificate structure, while a client-side web application employs a tile-based storage model to support independent cryptographic verification. Experimental evaluations have demonstrated the system's ability to deterministically detect any retroactive tampering with records. The fail-closed architecture also succeeded in categorically preventing the issuance of any unverified certificates during server failure simulations. On the operational level, performance measurements confirmed that this integration adds a delay of less than one second to the issuance cycle, with a linear growth in hash tile storage of 32 bytes per added certificate. These results confirm that incorporating a Merkle Tree-based verification layer into enterprise infrastructure replaces trust assumptions with mathematical proofs, providing organizations with tamper-evident auditing capabilities without compromising operational efficiency.

title: Title: Multi-Scale Information Fusion of a Non-Linear Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-scale information fusion model designed to enhance prediction accuracy by integrating information from diverse scales. The core aim is to address the inherent challenges of complex data by employing a non-linear model that facilitates a deeper understanding and integration of these varying levels of detail. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts the weighting of different scale features based on the specific context of the data, leading to improved model performance across a range of applications. The model's architecture is built upon a combination of feature extraction, hierarchical modeling, and non-linear transformations to capture the intricate relationships within the data. The paper details the model's design, training procedure, and validation results, demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting complex patterns. This work represents a significant advancement in multi-scale data integration, offering a robust and adaptable solution for various analytical tasks.

title: Graph Wavelets for Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to time series anomaly detection utilizing graph wavelets. Traditional methods frequently struggle to effectively identify anomalies within time series data characterized by intricate temporal dependencies. Our method leverages graph wavelets to transform time series data into a graph representation, where data points are nodes and temporal relationships are represented by edges. This graph structure is then analyzed using wavelet transforms, allowing for the detection of anomalies based on deviations from the expected graph structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique through a theoretical framework and explore its potential applications. The core claim is that traditional methods fail to capture complex temporal patterns, and this work proposes a solution using graph wavelets. This approach offers a more robust and accurate method for anomaly detection in time series data with complex relationships.

title: Multi-Modal Implicit Knowledge Graph Construction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to constructing knowledge graphs from implicit, multi-modal data. Traditional knowledge graph construction heavily relies on manual annotation, a process that is both time-consuming and expensive. Our method leverages the rich information contained within user behavior data – encompassing text, images, and videos – to automatically infer hidden knowledge and relationships. We employ deep learning models to represent these diverse modalities within a shared embedding space. Subsequently, we utilize similarity measures or graph neural networks to identify correlations and construct the knowledge graph. This approach significantly reduces the reliance on labeled data and offers a scalable solution for knowledge graph creation, particularly in scenarios where explicit knowledge bases are unavailable or incomplete. The core claim is that analyzing multi-modal user behavior data can effectively build a knowledge graph representing implicit knowledge and relationships. The key mechanism involves mapping different data modalities into a shared vector space using deep learning, followed by relationship discovery through similarity or graph neural networks. This work contributes to a more efficient and automated approach to knowledge graph construction, paving the way for intelligent applications that can reason and understand complex information.

title: Graph Neural Network Based Social Network Structure Prediction
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for predicting the structure and evolution of social networks. Traditional methods for social network analysis often rely on static network features and struggle to capture the dynamic nature of these complex systems. We propose a novel framework utilizing GNNs to learn the intricate patterns and relationships within social networks, enabling us to forecast future network configurations. The core mechanism involves constructing a GNN model that effectively integrates node and edge information to represent social network dynamics. The model then employs predictive algorithms to estimate the future state of the network. This approach represents a significant advancement in social network prediction, offering a more sophisticated and adaptable methodology compared to existing techniques. The research demonstrates the potential of GNNs to model and anticipate changes within social networks, with implications for various fields including social science, marketing, and public health.

title: Based on Biological Neural Networks for Explainable AI
abstract: This paper investigates the application of biologically inspired neural networks (BiNNs) to the field of Explainable AI (XAI). The core argument presented is that the inherent structure and function of BiNNs offer a natural pathway to constructing AI systems with intrinsic explainability. Traditional artificial neural networks (ANNs) often operate as "black boxes," making it difficult to understand the reasoning behind their decisions. In contrast, BiNNs, modeled after biological neural networks, possess features such as localized connections, adaptive dynamics, and inherent self-organization that lend themselves to greater transparency. This work proposes a framework for building XAI systems leveraging these characteristics. Specifically, we aim to simulate the synaptic connections and neuronal activity of biological networks to generate neural network models with explicitly interpretable components. Furthermore, we explore the utilization of BiNNs' self-organizing capabilities to enhance the transparency of the model's decision-making process. The presented approach addresses the growing need for AI systems that can not only produce accurate predictions but also provide understandable explanations for their outputs, fostering trust and accountability. The research focuses on the theoretical foundations and potential mechanisms of this novel approach, laying the groundwork for future development and experimentation.

title: Towards Automated Accessibility Adaptation of Learning Materials with Compact Large Language Models
abstract: This paper investigates the use of locally deployed Compact Large Language Models (CLLMs) to support inclusive education by automatically adapting learning materials for students with diverse accessibility needs. We propose a structured framework for multi-profile accessibility adaptation based on explicit, constraint-driven transformations, modeling learner profiles (e.g., dyslexia, ADHD, visual impairments) as sets of formalized requirements integrated into a modular pipeline. To support practical use, we also developed a web-based interface that allows users to input educational content, select a learner profile and a language model, and generate adapted versions of the text. We evaluate the framework using three locally executed models: Llama 3 8B, Mistral 7B, and Phi-3 Mini. title: Design a neuro-heuristic Morlet wavelet neural network procedure for the reactive transport system
abstract: This work shows the numerical performance through stochastic paradigms of the Reactive Transport System (RTS). The design of the solver is presented through the Morlet wavelet function, which works as an artificial neural network and the hybridization of a genetic algorithm and an active set. An objective function is created using the differential RTS, which is optimized through the hybrid capability of the designed scheme. The precision of the solver is perceived in comparison with the obtained and reference outcomes, the absolute error, and the number of multiple executions based on different operators. The inspiration to exploit the Morlet wavelet neural network process and the hybridization methods is to present precise and reliable solutions for solving the nonlinear and stiff differential systems. Three RTS cases are numerically treated to validate the efficiency of the designed process, and the performance of the scheme is also validated by using different statistical operators.

title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) is a critical task in telecom network operations, but diagnosing performance degradations in modern 5G and emerging 6G networks remains challenging due to complex cross-layer dependencies. While large language models (LLMs) offer promising capabilities for reasoning and knowledge integration, directly applying vanilla LLMs to telecom RCA often leads to hallucination, unstable reasoning, and poor alignment with structured network evidence. This work first reviews the evolution of telecom RCA from rule-based and machine learning (ML) approaches to emerging LLM-enabled techniques, and provides an overview of recent paradigms, including structured reasoning, retrieval-augmented knowledge grounding, agentic orchestration, and verifiable reasoning. Building upon these insights, we propose a structured reasoning framework for LLM-enabled telecom RCA that aligns diagnostic reasoning with telecom-specific evidence and domain knowledge. The proposed approach first organizes heterogeneous network telemetry into canonical contexts, and then enforces decision-path reasoning during diagnosis, and finally generates evidence-grounded explanations for reliable fault identification. Experimental results on two 5G RCA datasets, TeleLogs and TelecomTS, demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves diagnostic accuracy and decision consistency compared with baseline techniques. These cross-dataset results highlight the importance of structured reasoning design for practical LLM-based RCA systems in next-generation telecom networks.

title: Beauty is in the AI of the beholder: MLLMs systematically overrate facial attractiveness
abstract: Beauty assessments from Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly popular amongst users, companies, and aestheticians. This raises the question of whether these AI models can accurately reflect human judgments of attractiveness. In a pre- registered exploratory study, we compared the attractiveness ratings of 2,513 human participants to four widely used commercial AI models: Claude, Gemini, GPT, and Grok. Results showed that MLLMs systematically rate faces more favourably and within a narrower range than humans and, at the time of study, do not reproduce human ratings in absolute terms. However, MLLMs exhibit strong correlations with human attractiveness judgments, accurately tracking the rank-ordering of faces. MLLMs may judge faces by different cues than humans; only face age was a predictor of facial attractiveness in both humans and MLLMs, with inconsistent patterns across models for ethnicity and gender. AI models strongly agree with one another, except for Grok, which also showed the lowest agreement with humans. Our findings suggest that while they may be able to approximate rank-orderings of human attractiveness, current off-the-shelf commercial MLLMs systematically overrate the beauty of human faces.

title: Retrosynthesis of Synthetic Media for Explainable AI Provenance Forensics
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of generative models on Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) platforms, reliably tracing the provenance of synthetic media without modifying generator architectures or parameters remains a major challenge. In this work, we propose a self-referential retrosynthesis framework for explainable AI provenance forensics under a fixed-generator setting. The framework leverages a jointly optimized encoder-decoder pair to implement a self-embedding mechanism that enables round-trip consistency verification. During inference, client inputs are first encoded and then processed by the generator to produce outputs with high visual fidelity. For forensic verification, the consistency between the resynthesized image and the query image is analyzed to determine whether the image originates from the target generative model. Our approach eliminates the need for watermark embedding or modifications to the generation process. Experimental results show that images generated from encoded inputs maintain visual quality comparable to original generator outputs, while decoded images reliably trace back to their corresponding source inputs. Furthermore, the framework provides interpretable evidence for generative content provenance, establishing a practical tool for explainable generative AI forensics.

title: LaST-SR: Laplace-Inspired Steady-Transient Complex-Frequency Decomposition for Single Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Single-image super-resolution (SISR) requires global context modeling for structurally consistent reconstruction. Fourier operators are increasingly adopted for global feature modeling. However, their periodic spectral bases constrain the representation of localized aperiodic variations, limiting the recovery of irregular structures and fine details. In dynamical systems, the Laplace neural operator extends Fourier modes to complex frequencies and decomposes the output signal into complementary steady-state and transient responses to jointly model periodic and aperiodic information. We derive, for the first time, an approximate steady-transient decomposition for two-dimensional feature maps, providing an analytical basis for the proposed complex-frequency decomposition. Accordingly, we propose LaST-SR, centered on a Complex-Frequency Decomposition module that couples a global full-spectrum Fourier branch for image-wide dependencies and long-range structural consistency with a window-conditioned local complex-frequency branch for localized, content-dependent aperiodic variations. To fuse the resulting features, we further design a Steady-Transient Collaborative Aggregation module for cross-branch interaction and joint aggregation. Experiments on five benchmarks show that LaST-SR achieves the best PSNR/SSIM among the compared methods for $\times2$ and $\times4$ SISR. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed architecture and its key modeling mechanisms.

title: MCP Servers in Agentic AI - Architecture, Adoption, and Security of the Model Context Protocol
abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in late 2024, has emerged as a widely adopted open standard forconnecting large language model (LLM) applications to external tools, data sources, and services. By standardizing the interfacebetween an AI host application and the servers that expose capabilities to it, MCP has been described as a USB-C-like connectorfor agentic AI, replacing bespoke, one-off integrations with a single, reusable protocol. This paper explains how MCP servers work within agentic AI systems: the host-client-server architecture, the JSON-RPC 2.0 messaging layer, the core primitives of tools, resources, and prompts, and the rapid evolution of the specification from an initial local-only design to a stateless, horizontally scalable protocol core in its 2026-07-28 revision. We review the growing ecosystem of MCP servers and the parallel emergence of complementary agent-to-agent protocols, synthesize empirical security research documenting tool poisoning, indirect prompt injection, and auto-execution vulnerabilities across production AI coding tools, and summarize benchmarking efforts that evaluate LLM agents against real-world MCP server environments. We conclude with governance guidance for deploying MCP servers safely in production agentic systems and an agenda for future research.

title: Non-linear Topological Geometry Adaptive Constraint Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive constraint optimization techniques to complex systems, specifically focusing on non-linear topological geometry. The core idea centers around leveraging the inherent dynamism of topological structures to dynamically adjust constraints, enabling the identification of optimal solutions within complex, evolving systems. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with these structures, necessitating a novel approach that utilizes topological information to facilitate robust and adaptable solutions. We propose a new algorithm that integrates a "topological information" objective, dynamically adjusts constraint parameters based on the structure's evolution, and ultimately aims to find optimal solutions in complex systems. This research presents a framework for efficient and adaptive optimization, particularly relevant for systems requiring dynamic adjustment of constraints.

title: Dynamic Topology Spaces and Topology Migration Algorithms
abstract: Dynamic Topology Spaces (DTS) offers a novel approach to machine learning by leveraging the inherent adaptability of topological spaces. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Dynamic Topology Migration (DTM), designed to automatically transfer the structural characteristics of a source topology to a target topology. We propose a neural network architecture that learns a dynamic representation of the source topology and then iteratively migrates this representation to the target topology, enabling flexible and adaptable machine learning across diverse tasks and scenarios. This work addresses the limitations of static topology transfer methods by introducing a dynamic learning mechanism that allows the algorithm to continuously refine its representation and optimize performance. The proposed DTM demonstrates significant improvements in task performance and robustness compared to existing approaches, particularly in scenarios requiring significant structural change.

title: Dynamic Topology Search Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology search algorithm designed to enhance search efficiency. Traditional search algorithms often rely on manual design, limiting their adaptability. Our algorithm leverages the inherent properties of dynamic topology to dynamically adjust search strategies, resulting in improved performance. We present a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, focusing on optimizing the exploration of complex search spaces. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of topology through iterative refinement, providing a robust and adaptable solution for various search problems.

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Machine Learning for Constraint Optimization
abstract: Quantum-inspired machine learning offers a promising avenue for addressing complex constraint satisfaction problems, particularly those exhibiting inherent non-linearity and sensitivity to initial conditions. This paper explores the application of quantum-inspired techniques – specifically entanglement-based heuristics – to enhance the performance of machine learning algorithms used for constraint satisfaction. We propose a novel algorithm designed to intelligently guide the optimization process, aiming to accelerate solution finding and improve performance compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging the inherent properties of quantum mechanics to provide a computational advantage. This research investigates the potential of incorporating these features into existing machine learning frameworks to achieve significant improvements in constraint satisfaction scenarios. The goal is to provide a practical and efficient approach for tackling problems demanding rapid and accurate solution discovery.

title: Non-Locality in Quantum Simulation – Creating Systems with Robustness to Measurement Errors
abstract: Quantum simulation is a rapidly advancing field with immense potential for understanding and manipulating quantum systems. However, the inherent non-locality of quantum mechanics presents significant challenges, particularly when simulating complex quantum environments. This paper explores the problem of measurement errors, which can significantly compromise the accuracy of quantum simulations. We propose a novel design for quantum simulation algorithms that explicitly incorporate mechanisms to mitigate these errors, focusing on a proactive error correction strategy. The core claim is that by incorporating this mechanism, we can create more robust simulations capable of accurately reproducing the underlying quantum system, even in the presence of unavoidable measurement errors.

title: InfoBank ScenarioPacks S1-S6: An Author-Validated Synthetic Dataset for Governed Multi-Document Question Answering
abstract: InfoBank ScenarioPacks S1–S6 is an author-validated synthetic dataset for evaluating governed, multi-document question answering over user-controlled documents. It contains six self-contained scenario packages with 41 synthetic PDF documents and 42 annotated queries covering furniture care and proof of purchase, television documentation and warranty, grocery-order aggregation, order and bank-statement reconciliation, warranty versus household insurance, and electric-vehicle charging with home solar equipment. The scenarios test single- and multi-document retrieval, object-specific distractor rejection, evidence-grounded answers and citations, temporal and quantitative reasoning, governed aggregation, clarification, and refusal when evidence or the required aggregation threshold is insufficient. Each ZIP includes source PDFs, runtime-safe query inputs, policy fixtures, retrieval contracts, separate human-validated reference annotations, tabular summaries, manifests, and SHA-256 checksums. Runtime inputs are separated from reference answers to reduce evaluation leakage. All documents are synthetic, written in English, and contain no real personal data, credentials, account data, or financial records. Although developed for InfoBank, the packages can be adapted to other permission-aware RAG and personal document-assistant implementations. Names appearing in technical identifiers or synthetic documents do not imply affiliation or endorsement. Version 2.0 extends the original InfoBank ScenarioPacks S1–S6 dataset with a flattened 42-case question–reference-answer catalog. An InfoBank implementation is avaliable at https://github.com/gkusper/InfoBank.

title: Enhanced Security of Quantum Key Distribution Protocols Based on Quantum Phase Decoherence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to enhancing the security of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols by dynamically adjusting the estimation of quantum phase decoherence probability. Traditional QKD protocols often rely on static parameters, which limit their resilience against adaptive eavesdropping attacks. Our method leverages the real-time detection and mitigation of these attacks through the dynamic adjustment of decoherence probability estimation. Specifically, we introduce a feedback mechanism that monitors the estimated decoherence probability and adjusts key distribution parameters accordingly. This adaptive strategy provides a more robust defense against sophisticated attacks, ultimately improving the overall security of the QKD system. The core claim of this work is that dynamic adjustment of decoherence probability estimation can significantly bolster QKD security. The core mechanism relies on real-time attack detection and parameter adaptation. This approach represents a departure from the static parameter reliance of existing protocols, offering a proactive defense strategy.

title: Neural Network-Driven Program Generation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program generation utilizing simulated neural networks. The core concept involves training a neural network architecture to learn both algorithms and data patterns, subsequently enabling the automated creation of efficient code. Unlike traditional program synthesis methods, this research leverages the inherent pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks to directly translate high-level specifications into executable code. The system operates by mimicking human programming intuition and incorporating an algorithmic optimization process within the neural network structure. We explore the potential of this approach to accelerate software development and potentially discover novel algorithmic solutions. The architecture is designed to learn from both symbolic and numerical data, creating a robust and adaptable program generation system. This work presents a foundational framework for exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence and software engineering, offering a pathway toward intelligent code creation. The primary focus is on the conceptual design and theoretical underpinnings of the system, with future work planned to incorporate specific programming languages and evaluation methodologies.

title: A Distributed Proof System Based on Heterogeneous Computing Resources
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed proof system designed to leverage the parallel computing capabilities of heterogeneous computing resources, such as CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs, for efficient execution of complex mathematical proofs. The system addresses the limitations of existing distributed computing systems, which are primarily optimized for general-purpose computation and lack the specialized optimization required for mathematical reasoning. The core mechanism involves decomposing mathematical proofs into smaller, independent sub-problems, assigning these sub-problems to different heterogeneous computing resources for parallel solution, and then integrating the results through a distributed collaboration framework. The system's architecture is predicated on a modular design, allowing for adaptability to diverse proof methodologies and computational resource availability. This approach significantly reduces the computational burden associated with complex proofs, offering the potential for substantially faster proof generation and verification times. The theoretical framework incorporates concepts from distributed systems, parallel computing, and formal verification, providing a robust foundation for the system's design and implementation. We present a conceptual overview and outline key components of the system, highlighting its potential impact on areas such as theorem proving, automated reasoning, and cryptographic protocol analysis. ---

abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization algorithm based on high-dimensional non-linear geometry topology. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional data and require extensive parameter tuning. This algorithm leverages the inherent structure of geometric topologies to dynamically adjust optimization goals and parameters, leading to improved model optimization performance. We propose a "拓扑自适应优化" (Topology Adaptive Optimization) mechanism that dynamically connects the optimization process with the geometric topology of the problem, allowing for more effective model refinement. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved results across a range of benchmark datasets, highlighting the potential of this approach to tackle challenging optimization problems.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology Synthesis for Neural Networks
abstract: Dynamic Topology Synthesis (DTS) represents a novel approach to neural network layer design, focusing on automated generation and fine-tuning of network topologies to optimize for performance and robustness. This paper introduces a method leveraging a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to produce a "topology generator" capable of dynamically adapting to evolving data distributions. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop, iteratively refining the network architecture through adversarial training, ultimately aiming to achieve superior generalization and efficiency. The resulting system demonstrates improved performance across a range of benchmark datasets, highlighting the potential of DTS to overcome limitations of traditional static architecture design.

title: Pigeons That Learn to Flank You: A Comparative Analysis Review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of game AI and NPCs as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: Quantum State Non-Linear Entanglement Computation
abstract: Quantum state non-linear entanglement computation is a burgeoning field with immense potential for advancing computational capabilities. This paper explores a novel computational model predicated on quantum entanglement, aiming to overcome the limitations of classical computation in processing complex non-linear quantum states. The core mechanism centers around leveraging entanglement's unique properties to facilitate efficient and highly complex operations on quantum states. This research focuses on the design of a quantum computing framework that utilizes entanglement to achieve computational speedups and offers a fundamentally different approach to problem-solving. The paper details the model's architecture, explores its potential for specific algorithms, and discusses its implications for future advancements in quantum computation.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Differential Equation Modeling of Dynamical Systems
abstract: Quantum-enhanced differential equation modeling offers a novel approach to understanding and predicting the behavior of complex dynamical systems. This paper explores the potential of incorporating quantum mechanics into the framework of differential equation modeling to achieve significantly enhanced computational efficiency and accuracy. We outline a new methodology utilizing quantum-enhanced algorithms to simulate the evolution of differential equations, demonstrating the ability to represent and analyze systems previously intractable with conventional methods. This research addresses a critical challenge in dynamical systems science – the computational burden associated with complex simulations – and proposes a promising pathway toward more robust and insightful modeling.

title: Integration eines hochintegrierten Quantenempfängers in ein Quantum Key Distribution System mit kontinuierlichen Variablen - QuNET+DECODE (optimized coherent receiver for cv-qkd systems)
abstract: Das Projekt QuNET+DECODE hatte die Entwicklung eines leistungsstarken, vollständig integrierten Quantenempfängers für die Quanten-Schlüsselverteilung mit kontinuierlichen Variablen (CV-QKD) sowie dessen nahtlose Einbindung in die bestehende QuNET-Infrastruktur zum Ziel. Aufbauend auf einer Vielzahl bestehender CV-QKD-Experimente, die sich durch vielfältige Modulationsformate und Homodyn-Detektionsverfahren auszeichnen, verfolgte das Konsortium folgende Ziele: (i) die Anforderungen an das optische Frontend und den Transimpedanzverstärker (TIA) für ein dualpolarisationsoptimiertes CV-QKD-Protokoll zu definieren, (ii) die Empfänger-Schnittstellen mit dem QuNET-CV-QKD-System zu validieren und (iii) Codierungen höherer Ordnung im Stokes-Raum für die polarisationsdiverse Schlüsselgenerierung zu untersuchen. Zu Projektanfang wurden detaillierte Empfängerspezifikationen (Spannungsversorgung, Datenüberwachungsschnittstelle, Platzbedarf, elektromagnetische Suszeptibilität) festgelegt und Schnittstellentests mit kommerziellen Detektoren durchgeführt. Spektrale Rauschmessungen zeigten einen linearen Rauschpegel und ein geeignetes Verhältnis von Quanten- zu klassischem Rauschen. In anschließenden Experimenten mit einem polarisationsdiversen 90°-Hybrid sowohl in Glasfaser- als auch in Freistrahlverbindungen wurden Polarisationsdrift, Übersprechen und die Auswirkungen paralleler DWDM-Kanäle charakterisiert, wobei die für den integrierten DECODE-Empfänger erwarteten Bedingungen nachgebildet wurden. Das im Rahmen des Projekts entwickelte integrierte Modul wies eine unzureichende Trennung zwischen Quanten- und elektronischem Rauschen auf, was seinen Einsatz im QuNET-Schlüsselversuch (SE4) ausschloss. Dies unterstreicht die Notwendigkeit einer weiteren Optimierung des Rauschverhaltens integrierter Detektoren in Folgeuntersuchungen. Auf theoretischer Ebene untersuchte das Projekt Terme höherer Ordnung bei der Kodierung im Stokes-Raum und fand dabei hybride Kommutationsrelationen, die neue Forschungsrichtungen zur Quanteninformationsverarbeitung mit Polarisationszuständen eröffnen könnten.

title: FORMING A BUBBLE IN THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE MARKET
abstract: The dynamics of the development of the artificial intelligence market has been studied, highlighting not only financial indicators, but also research and social activity. The dynamics of investments in the AI market has been analyzed. It has been established that in recent years there has been a rapid development of the artificial intelligence market. It is artificial intelligence that is becoming the main means of technological and economic development, in various areas, such as business, finance, medicine. artificial intelligence in these areas entails significant investments, due to the high level of expectations, regarding the future impact on the development of the world economy. However, along with the active development of technology, there is also an increase in fears and discussions about the possible formation of an economic bubble in the artificial intelligence market. It is substantiated that if we characterize the AI market, it is worth noting the growth in the value of technology companies, rapid and large-scale venture investments, and the constant emergence of new startups. All of this bears some resemblance to previous tech booms, as well as the dot-com bubble. The capital expenditures of companies for financing artificial intelligence and the dynamics of financing artificial intelligence infrastructure are estimated. An analysis of general trends in large investments in new technologies and AI is performed. Examples of economic bubbles in the AI market are given. A comparison of previous bubbles and the modern AI market is carried out, common characteristics and differences are highlighted. Problems and risks of the development of the AI market are indicated. In the process of research, methods of comparative analysis, generalization of scientific approaches, as well as research of modern trends in the development of the technology sector were used, analysis of international economic data and reports, as well as research of modern literature on economic and technological bubbles.

title: VIS-DICT: A Visual Dictionary for Missing Modality Imputation in Social Network Depression Detection
abstract: Tracking social media posts can help spot early signs of depression. Recent studies show that combining text and images works better for detecting depression than using text alone. However, many social media posts do not have images, which makes it hard to use multimodal models. Most existing methods fill in missing images using retrieval or generative models that need extra training. In this paper, we introduce Vis-Dict, a dictionary-based method that builds missing visual features by linking words to average image vectors from complete training posts. These estimated visual features are then combined with text to track changes in user behavior over time. We tested Vis-Dict on a social media dataset using user timelines of up to 512 posts and compared it with other missing-data methods. The results show that Vis-Dict performs on par with generative networks, reaching an F1-score of 0.9454 and an ROC-AUC of 0.9890. Most importantly, Vis-Dict achieves this strong performance with zero trainable parameters for image generation. These findings show that directly connecting words to visual features is an effective and practical way to handle missing images in depression detection systems.

title: frb100-40 After Two Decades: An Optimality Certificate and a Preregistered Search Study
abstract: For more than 20 years, the Model-RB benchmark frb100-40 remained an open challenge; since 2014, its public record had stood at 99 of 100 variables. We give a directly checkable 100-vertex independent set for its 4,000-vertex graph. Together with a verified partition into 100 cliques of size 40, the witness proves that the maximum independent-set size is 100 and the minimum vertex-cover size is 3,900. The stochastic run that found the witness is kept separate from this proof. We evaluated its added pair and triple repair operators in a preregistered campaign comprising 8,668 valid runs. The primary comparison found no detectable acceleration over base ULSA (hazard ratio 0.967, 95% confidence interval 0.915-1.023; p=0.248), and the factorial ablation reached the same conclusion. On a smaller FRB suite, the group-aware CSP pipeline solved 2,500/2,500 runs, compared with 2,391/2,500 for LibMVC-NuMVC. On frb100-40, full ULSA, base ULSA, and NuMVC each produced 0/56 new certificates. With no events, the planned cross-solver hazard ratios remain unidentified. NuMVC ended with cover size 3,902 in 40 runs and 3,903 in 16. Exhaustive enumeration showed that none of the 108 unique recorded conflict-two states had a strictly improving group-aware CSP neighbor within Hamming radius three. The certificate settles the instance. The experiments characterize the search barrier, and the preregistered comparisons show no heuristic advantage.

title: Graph-MambaNav: Spatial-Temporal Graph Mamba Leveraging Object-Relation Knowledge for Object-Goal Navigation
abstract: Object-goal navigation requires an agent to reason over object relationships and prioritize target-relevant objects for efficient decision making in unseen environments. While existing graph-based methods incorporate target-awareness at the feature or attention level, they remain permutation-invariant and lack an explicit mechanism to control information propagation order, limiting their ability to model target-dependent importance and long-range dependencies. In contrast, Graph-Mamba highlights that node prioritization through sequence ordering is critical for effective global reasoning. In this work, we investigate the node prioritization mechanism in Graph-Mamba and study its role in object navigation. We propose Graph-MambaNav, a target-aware spatial-temporal graph encoding framework that introduces a heuristic ordering over objects based on their relevance to the target, allowing more informative objects to be processed later to aggregate richer context. Both node ordering and edge weights are initialized from LLM-derived commonsense object relationships, providing a unified prior for structured reasoning. A spatial module integrates local message passing with global GraphMamba-based selective scanning, while a temporal module applies Mamba-based sequence modeling over object-wise temporal orders, allowing selective aggregation of historical context for long-range temporal reasoning. Experiments on AI2-THOR and RoboTHOR demonstrate improved navigation performance with generalization, and additional real-world robot deployment further validates the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

title: PREDICTIVE AI FOR PERSONALIZED SECOND LANGUAGE LEARNING: DEVELOPING A DIGITAL MODEL TO PREDICT LEARNER DIFFICULTIES AND OPTIMIZE LANGUAGE INSTRUCTION
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), learning analytics, and adaptive educational technologies has created new opportunities for personalized second language (L2) learning. Traditional language instruction often relies on standardized curricula and periodic assessments, which may not adequately identify individual learners’ difficulties before they become persistent. Predictive artificial intelligence (Predictive AI) enables the analysis of learner-generated data, the identification of patterns associated with learning difficulties, the prediction of potential learning problems, and the recommendation of appropriate instructional interventions. This study aims to develop a conceptual digital model for Predictive AI-supported personalized second language learning. A conceptual-analytical research design was employed, involving the analysis and synthesis of recent studies on artificial intelligence in language education, adaptive learning, learning analytics, intelligent tutoring systems, learner profiling, personalized instruction, and self-regulated learning. The analysis indicates that AI-supported language learning can provide individualized feedback, adaptive learning pathways, diagnostic assessment, and personalized learning resources. However, existing research has placed greater emphasis on automated feedback and intelligent tutoring systems than on predictive learner profiling and the early identification of learning difficulties. Based on these findings, the study proposes the Predictive AI Personalized Language Learning Model (PAI-PLL Model), which comprises six interconnected stages: learner data collection, learner profiling, difficulty prediction, personalized recommendation, adaptive instruction, and continuous monitoring. The model integrates linguistic, behavioral, performance-based, and learning-process indicators while emphasizing teacher oversight and the ethical use of data. The proposed model conceptualizes Predictive AI as a decision-support mechanism rather than an autonomous replacement for teachers. Its principal contribution lies in integrating predictive analytics and personalized L2 instruction into a continuous preventive learning cycle. The model provides a theoretical and methodological foundation for future empirical research aimed at developing intelligent language-learning environments capable of identifying learner difficulties at an early stage and optimizing instructional decision-making.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit Design with Dynamic Resource Allocation
abstract: Quantum circuit design presents a significant challenge in the field of quantum computing, demanding efficient and robust circuit layouts. Static circuit layouts are often limited by the inherent complexity of quantum systems and can hinder optimization for both fidelity and speed. This research explores a novel adaptive quantum circuit design approach utilizing dynamic resource allocation. We propose a system that dynamically allocates quantum resources (qubits, gates) during circuit construction, optimizing for both fidelity and speed. The proposed framework leverages a 'resource allocation scheduling' algorithm that intelligently manages resources based on problem complexity and current system state. This system aims to address a key bottleneck in quantum circuit design – moving beyond static layouts to adaptive resource allocation, potentially unlocking significant improvements in both circuit fidelity and computational speed. This work presents a complete theoretical and practical implementation of this approach, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulation and preliminary experimentation. The focus is on creating a system that can intelligently manage the resources required for quantum circuit construction, leading to more efficient and robust designs.

Traditional topology-informed control often relies on static mappings, failing to effectively capture the dynamic behavior of complex systems. This work proposes a method that automatically adjusts the topology structure of the system during learning, enabling precise modeling and control of system behavior. The core mechanism involves a "topology mapping" process, which iteratively refines the system's topology to match the desired target state. This adaptive approach offers a significant improvement over existing methods by providing a more flexible and robust framework for system modeling and control. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of simulations, showcasing its ability to accurately represent and manipulate system dynamics.

title: Title: Algorithmic Complexity of Cognitive Networks via Quantum Simulation
abstract: Cognitive networks, mimicking the human brain, exhibit complex interactions and emergent behaviors. Traditional complexity measures, while useful, often fail to adequately represent the subtle quantum-influenced processes underpinning reasoning and learning. This paper investigates the algorithmic complexity of cognitive networks through a novel quantum simulation approach, aiming to quantify and potentially enhance the network's inherent complexity. We propose a quantum algorithm designed to explore the potential state space of the network, revealing underlying quantum-enhanced reasoning pathways. The research seeks to provide a deeper, more nuanced understanding of cognitive systems by utilizing the principles of quantum mechanics. This work addresses a critical gap in our understanding of how quantum phenomena might influence network dynamics.

title: Dynamic Topology for Quantum Information Encoding and Puzzle Solving
abstract: Dynamic topology, a fascinating field of mathematics, offers a novel approach to quantum information processing. This paper explores the potential of dynamically evolving topological structures to enhance quantum information encoding and puzzle-solving capabilities. We investigate a specific algorithm leveraging dynamic topology to generate and manipulate quantum states, fostering a novel approach to quantum computation. The core mechanism involves the application of dynamic topology to create entangled states with enhanced properties, ultimately leading to more efficient and secure quantum computation. The research focuses on a particular quantum puzzle – a variation of the game of Nim – where dynamic topology facilitates the development of complex, unpredictable patterns. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in generating intricate puzzle solutions, showcasing a significant advancement in quantum algorithm design. This work represents a significant step toward harnessing the inherent properties of dynamic topology for advanced quantum technologies.

title: Quantum-Guided Optimization for Non-Linear Systems
abstract: Quantum-Guided Optimization (QGO) represents a novel approach to solving complex optimization problems, particularly those exhibiting non-linear characteristics. This paper introduces a framework for optimizing non-linear systems utilizing quantum entanglement, aiming to significantly accelerate and enhance traditional optimization techniques. We detail the core mechanism of QGO, outlining its architecture, quantum algorithm, and potential benefits in terms of computational efficiency and solution quality. The proposed method leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to facilitate the exploration of the solution space and guide the optimization process towards optimal configurations. The paper provides a comprehensive discussion of the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of QGO.

title: Probabilistic Verification of Concurrent Programs with Abstract Interpretation
abstract: Concurrent program verification remains a significant challenge due to the inherent complexities arising from interactions between multiple processes. Traditional static analysis techniques, including abstract interpretation, often struggle to capture the full range of possible concurrent behaviors, leading to false negatives—verifying programs that actually exhibit undesirable behavior. This paper proposes a novel approach that combines abstract interpretation with probabilistic models to provide a more rigorous verification framework. We introduce an extension to abstract interpretation that incorporates probabilistic representations of concurrent execution, allowing us to quantify and reason about uncertainties in synchronization and communication. The core idea is to represent program states not as single values but as probability distributions, reflecting the likelihood of different execution paths. This approach significantly improves the ability to detect subtle concurrency errors that would otherwise be missed by deterministic abstract interpretation. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this method through a detailed theoretical analysis and illustrate its application with a simplified example. The key contribution lies in the formal integration of probabilistic models into the abstract interpretation process, offering a more nuanced and accurate representation of concurrent program behavior. ---

title: Quantum Phase Field Simulation: Adaptive Optimization for Enhanced Simulation
abstract: Quantum phase field (QPF) simulations offer a powerful tool for studying complex quantum systems, particularly in areas such as condensed matter physics and quantum materials. However, traditional QPF simulations often require extensive parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and limit the exploration of the parameter space. This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization algorithm for QPF simulations, designed to automatically adjust simulation parameters based on the resulting data, thereby significantly improving simulation accuracy and efficiency. The algorithm leverages the inherent dynamics of quantum phase field simulations to dynamically adjust parameters, ensuring a robust and efficient simulation process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a series of simulations, showcasing its ability to achieve superior results compared to existing optimization techniques.

title: Bayesian Networks for High-Dimensional Data Anomaly Detection Framework
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for high-dimensional data anomaly detection leveraging Bayesian Networks (BNs). The core idea is to represent complex, high-dimensional data as a BN, enabling probabilistic inference to identify anomalies based on deviations from learned dependencies. This approach offers advantages over traditional methods by explicitly modeling relationships between variables and providing interpretable anomaly explanations. The framework utilizes probability distributions to determine the likelihood of data points belonging to normal patterns, and then performs causal analysis to identify the root causes of anomalies. We explore the application of BNs for anomaly detection, demonstrating their ability to handle intricate data dependencies and provide insights into the underlying reasons for anomalous behavior. The framework's key contributions lie in its ability to effectively model high-dimensional data and offer a transparent and explainable approach to anomaly detection.

title: Quantum Simulation of Topology Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum simulation, focusing on the development of a method for modeling quantum simulation based on topological structure. The core claim is that this method will generate more efficient simulations and reveal complex structures within quantum systems. Traditional quantum simulation often relies on classical methods, limiting our ability to capture the intricate structure of quantum systems. Topology modeling offers a unique avenue for simulating these structures directly, reducing simulation errors and significantly enhancing simulation accuracy. This work explores the design of a computational framework predicated on topological structure, aiming to minimize error and improve simulation fidelity. We present a foundational mechanism involving the inherent properties of topological structures, leading to a more precise and efficient simulation process. The resulting system will be capable of generating more accurate and insightful visualizations of quantum system behavior.

title: 基于量子噪声的量子密钥分发协议
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol leveraging the inherent characteristics of quantum noise. The core claim is that exploiting quantum noise can significantly enhance the security of QKD. The proposed protocol utilizes the random nature of quantum noise to introduce disturbances for eavesdropping attempts, ultimately improving key distribution security. The protocol's design focuses on mitigating the impact of channel noise while maintaining key rate. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and outline the key components of the system. The protocol's effectiveness is analyzed through mathematical modeling, demonstrating its potential for robust key exchange in noisy environments. The analysis highlights the trade-offs between key rate and security, a crucial consideration in practical QKD implementations.

title: Homomorphic Encryption for Privacy-Preserving Data Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the application of homomorphic encryption (HE) to enable privacy-preserving data analysis. Traditional methods of data analysis frequently necessitate decryption, introducing significant security vulnerabilities. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing HE to perform computations directly on encrypted data, effectively shielding the underlying data from exposure. The core claim is that HE allows for secure data analysis without decryption. The mechanism involves constructing a homomorphic encryption computing environment, employing HE algorithms for encryption and operations, ultimately facilitating safe analysis of sensitive data. This work investigates the feasibility and potential benefits of this approach, addressing the critical need for robust data privacy in increasingly data-driven environments. The primary contribution lies in demonstrating a practical framework for utilizing HE in data analysis scenarios, moving beyond theoretical concepts toward tangible security solutions. ---

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Adaptive Parameter Scaffolding
abstract: Training deep neural networks is often hampered by the accumulation of errors, leading to suboptimal performance and instability. This paper introduces a novel architecture, Adaptive Parameter Scaffolding (APS), designed to mitigate this problem through an intrinsic self-correcting mechanism. The core idea is to integrate a dynamically adjusting "scaffolding" network alongside the primary neural network. This scaffolding network continuously monitors the primary network's output and internal activations, identifying potential error signals and proactively adjusting the weights of the primary network to minimize these errors. The adjustment process is governed by a feedback loop, creating a self-correcting system. We present a theoretical framework for understanding the dynamics of this system, outlining key equations and mathematical relationships. The design emphasizes adaptability and real-time error correction, potentially leading to more robust and efficient training processes for deep neural networks. The proposed approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm compared to traditional training methods, shifting from passive adjustment to active error correction within the network itself.

title: Formal Specification and Verification of Quantum Computing Algorithms
abstract: The verification of quantum computing algorithms presents a significant hurdle due to the probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics and the complex entanglement inherent in quantum computations. This paper proposes a novel approach to address this challenge by developing a formal language and a corresponding verification tool tailored explicitly for quantum algorithm specification and verification. The system leverages concepts from quantum information theory and formal methods to provide a rigorous framework for ensuring the correctness of quantum algorithms. We introduce a new formalism that allows for precise description of quantum circuits and their operations, combined with automated theorem proving techniques to systematically verify the algorithm's behavior against a given specification. The key innovation lies in the ability to reason about quantum states and measurements within a formal setting, enabling a more comprehensive understanding and validation of these algorithms. This work lays the foundation for increased confidence in the development and deployment of quantum computing technologies.

title: Proceedings of the WGOS'26: Women & Girls' Online Safety Conference 2026
abstract: These proceedings collect the contributions presented at the Proceedings of the WGOS’26: Women & Girls’ Online Safety Conference, held on September 2026 at Milton Keynes. The volume brings together 54 contributions spanning four types: research papers, abstracts, posters and presentation proposals. Research papers and abstracts represent original work submitted and reviewed through our open call for papers, and describe novel technical solutions, evaluations of existing methods, or empirical studies. Posters present ongoing or practice-based work. Presentation proposals offer authors the opportunity to share previously published work with the conference audience; these contributions are not presented as original works and full references to the original publications are provided. Contributions are organised by type and listed in the table of contents. Each contribution has been assigned an individual digital object identifier (DOI) and is independently citable. The full proceedings, including all individual contributions, are available open access on Zenodo at https://zenodo.org/communities/cpwo-wgos-2026/

title: A Low-Resource Arabic Dataset and Transformer-Based Benchmark for Dark Pattern Detection in E-Commerce Mobile Applications
abstract: Arabic remains underrepresented in many task-specific natural language processing (NLP) resources and benchmarks, particularly for specialized user interface (UI) understanding tasks. In mobile commerce, Arabic UI text may contain persuasive or deceptive design cues known as dark patterns; however, Arabic-language dark pattern detection remains largely unexplored. To the best of our knowledge, this paper presents the first ML-based benchmark for Arabic dark pattern detection. We construct a novel annotated dataset of 223 Arabic UI text strings from nine e-commerce mobile applications operating in Saudi Arabia, labeled across five dark pattern categories and a non-dark-pattern class (Cohen’s kappa κ = 0.89). Using a stratified, leakage-free 70/10/20 split with parent-aware paraphrase augmentation applied only to the training partition, we fine-tune five pretrained transformer models: AraBERTv2, MARBERT, mBERT, BERT-base-uncased, and RoBERTa-base. Our primary evaluation is 5-fold cross-validation on the 223 original, non-augmented instances, separate from the augmented training corpus used for the held-out test comparison. Under this evaluation, MARBERT achieves the strongest performance (mean macro-F1 = 0.4230), numerically ahead of AraBERTv2 (0.2998) by a margin that does not reach statistical significance at five folds (p ≈ 0.064), and ahead of mBERT (0.3234); MARBERT significantly outperforms both English-only baselines, and mBERT is numerically stronger than both, though mBERT was not directly tested against them for significance. This suggests pre-training on dialectal, code-switched Arabic may matter more here than Arabic pre-training alone. Per-class analysis shows every model struggles with several minority categories, indicating Arabic dark pattern detection remains genuinely difficult at current data volumes. The annotated dataset is publicly released to support future low-resource Arabic NLP research.

title: MAOL: Morphology-Aware Ordinal Learning for Fine-Grained Industrial Defect Severity Grading
abstract: Fine-grained defect severity grading is essential for industrial inspection, yet remains challenging due to the ordinal nature of severity labels, the strong dependence on morphology-related cues, and the train-test discrepancy between clean annotated instances and noisy predicted instances in two-stage pipelines. We propose MAOL, a Morphology-Aware Ordinal Learning framework for fine-grained industrial defect severity grading. MAOL formulates severity grading as an instance-level ordinal learning task, incorporates explicit morphological features to enhance representation learning, introduces class-conditional adaptive ordinal thresholds to model defect-specific grading boundaries, and employs prediction-aware training via localization perturbation to improve robustness to imperfect predicted instances. Extensive experiments under both clean-ROI and predicted-instance settings demonstrate that MAOL consistently outperforms rule-based methods, nominal classification models, and existing ordinal baselines, especially in the predicted-instance setting. The proposed approach ranked third in the IDA 2026 Challenge on Fine-Grained Severity Grading for High-Precision Manufacturing.

title: SecureMed-FL: A Privacy- and Security-Aware Federated Learning Framework for Brain Tumor MRI Classification
abstract: SecureMed-FL is a privacy- and security-aware federated learning framework for brain tumor MRI classification across five simulated healthcare institutions. The framework integrates FedAvg and FedProx optimization, controlled non-IID heterogeneity, record-level differential privacy, black-box membership-inference auditing, and masking-based secure-aggregation simulation within a unified experimental pipeline. The study evaluates the trade-offs among predictive utility, heterogeneity robustness, privacy protection, empirical leakage, and aggregation efficiency in trustworthy federated medical imaging.

title: ZenBrain: Neuroscience-Inspired Agent Memory Library for LLM Agents
abstract: Source code release of ZenBrain, an open-source agent memory library for LLM agents: seven neuroscience-inspired memory layers (working, short-term, episodic, semantic, procedural, core, cross-context) behind a memory coordinator that stores, recalls, forgets and consolidates, and a library of 20 algorithm modules (10 core algorithms + 10 advanced research modules) such as FSRS spaced repetition, Hebbian learning and sleep replay. Which mechanisms the coordinator runs on its own and which the library offers as functions is listed in the repository README. TypeScript, Apache-2.0; the algorithm package has zero runtime dependencies. 822 automated tests, CI on Node 22, 24 and 26 and against PostgreSQL with pgvector. This record pins the exact released version: Git tag v0.5.1 (commit 12d9076f) Source archive in this record: zenbrain-v0.5.1.tar.gz, SHA-256 a65a6f59728a54c98a9646990be5d97d63730d94c545215c478599b08854a503 npm: @zensation/algorithms@0.5.1 — dist SHA-1 bc4ccce27d9c3117c872c0fe9b43ef91de2aa6d3, 153 files; @zensation/core@0.5.1 and @zensation/mcp@0.2.1 from the same tag Relation to the paper (arXiv:2604.23878): the architecture described there comprises 15 neuroscience-inspired mechanisms — 9 foundational algorithms plus 6 Predictive Memory Architecture (PMA) components. The 6 PMA components are proprietary and run in the production system; this open-source package ships the algorithm library (20 modules). The two counts describe different things and are both stated in the paper and the repository README.

Which mechanisms the coordinator runs on its own and which the library offers as functions is listed in the repository README. TypeScript, Apache-2.0; the algorithm package has zero runtime dependencies. 822 automated tests, CI on Node 22, 24 and 26 and against PostgreSQL with pgvector. This record pins the exact released version: Git tag v0.5.1 (commit 12d9076f) Source archive in this record: zenbrain-v0.5.1.tar.gz, SHA-256 a65a6f59728a54c98a9646990be5d97d63730d94c545215c478599b08854a503 npm: @zensation/algorithms@0.5.1 — dist SHA-1 bc4ccce27d9c3117c872c0fe9b43ef91de2aa6d3, 153 files; @zensation/core@0.5.1 and @zensation/mcp@0.2.1 from the same tag Relation to the paper (arXiv:2604.23878): the architecture described there comprises 15 neuroscience-inspired mechanisms — 9 foundational algorithms plus 6 Predictive Memory Architecture (PMA) components. The 6 PMA components are proprietary and run in the production system; this open-source package ships the algorithm library (20 modules). The two counts describe different things and are both stated in the paper and the repository README.
