title: Quantum Decoherence-Based Cryptanalysis Method
abstract: This paper introduces a novel cryptanalysis method leveraging the principles of quantum decoherence. The core idea centers on exploiting the controllable nature of decoherence times within quantum bits (qubits) to identify vulnerabilities in quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. Specifically, we propose a method for pinpointing critical operations that induce decoherence, ultimately leading to key leakage and, potentially, the breaking of the underlying encryption algorithms. The approach distinguishes itself from existing QKD attacks by directly targeting the decoherence process itself, offering a new direction for cryptanalysis in the quantum realm. The presented framework provides a theoretical foundation and outlines a strategy for developing more effective attacks against QKD systems.

title: Adaptive Optimization Based on Biofeedback
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithm optimization leveraging biofeedback signals. The core idea is to dynamically adapt algorithm parameters and strategies in real-time by monitoring and analyzing human physiological signals such as electroencephalogram (EEG) and heart rate variability (HRV). This adaptive process utilizes a feedback loop, where the biofeedback data is correlated with algorithm performance, a machine learning model learns the relationship between the signals and algorithm parameters, and the model automatically adjusts the parameters to enhance optimization efficiency. Unlike traditional optimization methods that rely on manual intervention or fixed strategies, this system offers a dynamic and personalized optimization process, potentially leading to significantly improved results. The system architecture, learning methodology, and theoretical framework are detailed within this document.

title: Dynamic Topological Learning for Adaptive Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of dynamic topological learning (DTL) algorithms to revolutionize quantum computing. The core claim is that quantum computers can leverage DTL to optimize quantum circuit structures, ultimately achieving computational advantages over classical computers. The proposed mechanism utilizes quantum entanglement and superposition to construct a topological representation of the circuit, iteratively refining connections through quantum decoherence and measurement. This adaptive approach overcomes the limitations of fixed-structure quantum algorithms, offering a pathway to dynamic problem adaptation and accelerated solution times. The research focuses on developing a framework for DTL in quantum computing, highlighting the opportunities for enhanced parallel processing and reduced computational complexity. The presented methodology addresses a critical need for adaptable quantum algorithms, paving the way for more efficient and versatile quantum computation. This work establishes a theoretical foundation for DTL and its application within the quantum computing landscape, anticipating future advancements in quantum algorithm design and execution.

title: Quantum Entanglement Topological Computation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum computation leveraging the topological properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim is to construct a highly fault-tolerant distributed computing architecture by harnessing these topological features, thereby mitigating the decoherence challenges prevalent in traditional quantum computing. The proposed mechanism involves encoding quantum information into physically interconnected quantum nodes via entangled networks. This topological protection inherently provides redundancy for quantum information storage and facilitates error correction. Furthermore, the architecture utilizes the inherent topology of the nodes for parallel computation. The resulting system offers a fundamentally different paradigm for quantum computing, promising scalability and robustness. The theoretical framework presented outlines the key components and operational principles, focusing on the manipulation and utilization of entangled states within a topological framework. The primary goal is to demonstrate a pathway towards building practical, resilient quantum computers capable of tackling complex computational problems. This work establishes a foundational model for future research in entanglement-based topological quantum computation.

title: Trustworthy Reinforcement Learning for AI-Driven Urban Decision-Making: Sustainable Dynamic Pricing and Resource Optimization for Smart City Operations
abstract: Rapid urbanization, increasing demand variability, and digitalisation of urban infrastructure require intelligent decision-support systems that can improve sustainability, resilience, and operational efficiency in smart city operations. Artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven optimization offer strong potential for adaptive urban services, including dynamic pricing, demand response, resource allocation, and energy-aware management. However, many reinforcement learning applications still focus mainly on short-term performance while giving limited attention to transparency, fairness, stability, and accountability. This study proposes a trustworthy reinforcement learning framework for AI-driven urban decision-making, using sustainable dynamic pricing and resource optimization as mechanisms for adaptive and responsible decision-making. A custom reinforcement learning environment was developed using historical e-commerce transactional data as a methodological proxy to simulate interactions among demand, resource or inventory availability, service categories, price elasticity, and changing market conditions. Three reinforcement learning algorithms, namely Deep Q-Network, Proximal Policy Optimization, and Advantage Actor–Critic, were evaluated under comparable experimental conditions. Performance was assessed using profitability, decision stability, fairness-oriented pricing behavior, decision consistency, and interpretability. To improve transparency, trajectory-based policy audits and SHapley Additive exPlanations were applied to identify the main factors influencing pricing decisions. The results show that the Deep Q-Network agent achieved the most balanced performance, increasing total profit by 12.58% while recording no unethical price increases under low-demand conditions. Explainability analysis showed that stock or resource levels, demand shifts, and price elasticity were the strongest positive drivers of pricing actions, whereas inventory hoarding and unfavorable price increases reduced decision quality. The findings indicate that reinforcement learning can support sustainable and resilient urban decision-making when optimization objectives are combined with trustworthy AI principles. The proposed framework provides a practical basis for accountable AI-based decision-support systems in smart city operations, including demand-responsive services, resource optimization, sustainable dynamic pricing, and energy-aware management.

title: Consensus Bayesian Network Learning for Market Basket Analysis in Indonesian Retail Transactions
abstract: Understanding relationships among products in retail transactions is essential for supporting strategic decisions such as product placement and cross-selling. However, traditional market basket analysis is limited to pairwise associations and cannot capture complex conditional dependencies among multiple items. This study addresses these limitations by applying a Bayesian Network framework to model product relationships probabilistically. Transaction data collected over one month were transformed into a binary dataset of 441 transactions across 31 product categories. The network structure was learned using a stochastic search algorithm with a Bayesian Dirichlet equivalent (BDe) score, enhanced by a multi-seed strategy and edge support aggregation to ensure robustness. Parameters were estimated using maximum likelihood. The results indicate that relationships are both directional and context-dependent, with snack probabilities increasing with instant noodles but decreasing when cigarettes are also present. The LOIO accuracy is 0.6659.

title: Topology-aware GNNs under structural perturbations: Empirical robustness across domains
abstract: Graph neural networks learn from relational structure but can be sensitive to edge-level noise. We study a hybrid graph classifier that combines a message-passing branch (Graph Isomorphism Network, GIN) with a topological branch based on extended persistence diagrams and PersLay embeddings. Training optionally uses a paper-specific hinge penalty motivated by stable persistence-diagram representations and Lipschitz regularity, which we abbreviate as “HK-inspired.” On six TUDataset benchmarks, we compare five ablations (Full, GIN+PersLay, GIN + HK, GIN only, PersLay only) and measure robustness as accuracy drop under 10% random edge removal at test time, with persistence diagrams fixed from the original graphs; we also report targeted perturbations on MUTAG and PROTEINS and runtime on all six datasets. The regularized configurations reduce relative accuracy degradation where GIN-only is sensitive, particularly on smaller molecular and protein graphs, but do not consistently maximize clean or perturbed accuracy. On large social-network benchmarks, robustness differences are small and clean accuracy is the main differentiator. Adding PersLay to GIN can improve accuracy on several datasets, while PersLay alone performs worst. Training the full model increases per-epoch cost relative to GIN-only, with most overhead during training rather than inference. Overall, the results support a conditional empirical conclusion: combining structure, topology, and stability-oriented training can improve robustness under specified structural perturbations, with dataset-dependent accuracy–stability trade-offs rather than universal guarantees.

title: Computing with qLDPC Codes by Climbing the Chain Map Hierarchy
abstract: We develop a framework for logical computation with qLDPC codes that places logical Pauli, Clifford, and non-Clifford operations on the same footing. This brings the simple homological description of Pauli logicals to the patchwork landscape of logical Clifford and non-Clifford operations, providing a tool for the discovery of new logical gates. In particular, we define the chain map hierarchy: a family of chain complexes whose homology classes encode logical unitary and code surgery operations at any level of the Clifford hierarchy, precisely analogous to the chain complex description of Pauli logicals. Consequently, intuition for Pauli logicals can be leveraged to discover new logical operations on qLDPC codes. For instance, the familiar ability to deform Pauli logicals with stabilizers---i.e. boundaries of the chain complex---becomes a way to search for constant-depth unitary implementations of (non-)Clifford logical gates. Using this strategy, we discover constant-depth unitary implementations of the full logical Clifford group on any number of blocks of the 2D toric code, including within a single block, and addressable logical CCZ gates on any triple of logical qubits on any number of blocks of the 3D toric code. Beyond manifold codes, we find addressable non-Clifford gates on codes with many encoded qubits. The chain map hierarchy naturally encompasses and extends other constructions of logical gadgets, for instance providing a universal parameterization of cup products. As such, our work provides a unified, useful, and intuitive language for computing with qLDPC codes.

title: Training seeds and model-selection stability in recommender-system evaluation
abstract: Recommender-system experiments often rely on a single random training seed, assuming that run-to-run stochasticity has limited impact on evaluation conclusions. This assumption is risky, as a training seed may influence several algorithm-dependent mechanisms, including parameter initialization, mini-batch ordering, dropout, masking, latent sampling, and training-time negative sampling. We examine this assumption by fixing the data partition and varying the training seed across hyperparameter configurations. We analyze seed effects at three levels: user-level metric sensitivity, validation-based model selection and recommendation-list agreement. Results show that seed variation is often detectable. Its impact depends on whether configurations are clearly separated, whether validation results transfer to test, and whether similar scores lead to similar top-$k$ lists. Findings suggest that reporting single-seed results can overstate the stability of recommender system evaluation, and that training seeds should be treated as part of the evaluation protocol rather than as incidental implementation noise.

title: T2LSC-Bench: Benchmarking Localized Semantic Control in Text-to-Image Generation
abstract: Recent text-to-image models have become increasingly capable of rendering explicit text, but reliable localized text control requires more than generating the correct string. In applications such as product labeling, signage, and interface design, target text should be rendered within a designated text-bearing region without altering the predefined subject identity or surrounding scene semantics. We refer to violations of this requirement as target-text-associated semantic leakage, in which target-text semantics are expressed through non-textual visual content beyond the designated anchor. Existing visual-text benchmarks primarily evaluate readability, spelling accuracy, and layout, leaving this form of semantic leakage largely unexamined. We introduce T2LSC-Bench, a controlled diagnostic benchmark comprising 50 seed subjects and 1,200 prompt cases per model, yielding 7,160 evaluated images across six models. Its factorized design varies semantic relation, scene openness, prompt mode, and language. A dual-branch protocol combines OCR-VLM text verification with structured VLM semantic judgments to measure Text-at-Anchor Accuracy (TAA), Semantic Subject Preservation (SSP), Semantic Leakage Rate (SLR), and Conditional Semantic Leakage Rate (cSLR). Under stress-test conditions, SLR increases from 1.2% to 18.1% and cSLR from 1.3% to 18.2%, whereas TAA decreases only from 91.4% to 90.9%. Anti-leakage prompting reduces SLR from 16.6% to 8.4% without degrading rendering accuracy. Human validation on 420 images shows strong agreement between automatic and adjudicated annotations. These results show that accurate text rendering does not guarantee local containment of target-text semantics.

title: Group-Aware Adaptive Retrieval for Evidence Navigation
abstract: Reasoning-intensive retrieval addresses queries whose relevance cannot be identified by surface-level matching, thereby requiring multi-step reasoning. Because relevant documents rarely appear in the initial candidate set, retrieval systems suffer from the bounded recall problem. Existing methods iteratively expand a candidate pool at the document level over a corpus graph, examining each neighbor in isolation and drifting toward a narrow region of the corpus. To address this problem, we propose Group-Aware Adaptive Retrieval for Evidence Navigation (GAREN), which explores the corpus graph through group-level expansion. GAREN organizes documents into semantically coherent and distinguishable groups based on their connections in the corpus graph. The information in each group indicates what can be accessed by expanding through it, providing guidance beyond individual document-level signals. At each iteration, GAREN uses a group-level navigator to identify promising expansion directions, retrieves documents from the selected groups, and applies a document-level reranker to evaluate the updated candidate set. Extensive experiments show that GAREN achieves up to 8.0% improvement over the strongest baseline on BRIGHT. The source code is available at https://github.com/KJ12124/GAREN

title: Privacy Washing: Detecting Internal Contradictions in Privacy Policies
abstract: Privacy policies may contain internal contradictions in which commitments are undermined by practices documented elsewhere in the same policy. We operationalize this phenomenon, privacy washing, through a four-stage pipeline: statement extraction, compatibility filtering and natural language inference screening, multi-model judge verification, and thematic analysis, with contradictions confirmed by majority vote of a three-model LLM panel. Applied to two corpora of website privacy policies, 123 collected in 2026 (OPPT) and 115 collected in 2015 (OPP-115), the pipeline finds the same category patterns recurring across the 11-year gap, with third-party sharing contradictions the majority of confirmed cases in each primary run, consistent with structural factors in policy composition rather than necessarily intentional deception. At least one panel-confirmed contradiction appears in 12.2% of OPPT companies (15/123; 9.8% excluding legacy pairs) and 36.5% of OPP-115 companies (42/115). A stability re-run seven months later, with a fully separated configuration (new extraction models, judges from three Chinese providers absent from both corpora, matched filters, no judge-submission similarity threshold), reproduces the OPPT prevalence under the original protocol (13.0% vs. 12.2%), finds sub-threshold pairs confirm at rates of the same order as those above (raising prevalence to 20.3% and 40.9%), and shows the third-party majority is panel-sensitive while the recurrence of the same category pairs is not. Two caveats govern all figures: panel verdicts are not validated against human expert judgment, so precision is unknown and prevalence figures are lower bounds; and the two primary runs used different filter configurations, so their prevalence difference is not interpretable as a corpus or era effect (the matched re-run reduces the gap to roughly twofold but does not eliminate it).

title: The Most Accurate AI Translator in 2026 - 10 AI models tested on legal, medical, idiom, and formality translations
abstract: Two words, six models, three different translation calls. This MachineTranslation.com article runs 8 test sentences, covering idioms, formality, legal and medical terminology, and deliberate ambiguity, through 10 AI models translating English to Japanese and English to Vietnamese, exposing where models silently agree and where they diverge in ways invisible to anyone reading only one output. The starkest finding: a Vietnamese medical term that stays split 6 to 4 even after expanding the model pool. The takeaway isn't which model is "best," it's knowing when model disagreement signals that human review is needed, which is exactly what MachineTranslation.com's multi-model consensus makes visible.

The takeaway isn't which model is "best," it's knowing when model disagreement signals that human review is needed, which is exactly what MachineTranslation.com's multi-model consensus makes visible.

title: Augmented or Undermined? The Positive and Negative Effects of Generative AI on Product Management: A Rapid Structured Review
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly entering product-management work through research synthesis, ideation, requirements drafting, artifact evaluation, analytics, and stakeholder communication. This rapid structured review examines when GenAI augments product judgment and when it undermines it. Eighteen candidate publications were screened through 2 September 2026, of which sixteen were retained: three direct product-management empirical studies, six product and innovation contextual sources, and seven adjacent empirical studies from knowledge work and software development. The evidence identifies benefits including faster completion of bounded tasks, repeatable critique, idea expansion, improved knowledge access, and support for less-experienced workers. Reported risks include inaccurate outputs, overreliance, homogenization, reduced critical-thinking effort, skill erosion, weakened peer interaction, privacy concerns, and diffused accountability. The paper proposes an AI–PM Dual-Impact Framework based on task–model fit, grounding, expertise, verification, human ownership, and organizational support. The findings support selective, governed adoption rather than universal automation. This manuscript is a preprint and has not undergone peer review. The supporting screening and evidence-extraction tracker accompanies the paper.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Geometry Transformation
abstract: Quantum State Adaptive Geometry Transformation is a novel approach to system optimization that leverages the dynamic nature of quantum states. This method proposes a system of geometric transformations, driven by the inherent quantum properties of the system, to automatically adjust the system's structure, thereby enhancing adaptability and stability. Traditional physics models rely on classical laws, while this approach harnesses the dynamic behavior of quantum states for automatic geometric restructuring. This research explores the potential of this technique to address challenges in complex systems, particularly those exhibiting intricate dependencies and requiring adaptive responses. The core mechanism involves continuous, self-adjusting geometric transformations, achieved through a carefully designed framework of quantum state manipulation. This paper presents a detailed analysis of the proposed approach, including mathematical formulations and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in a simplified scenario.

title: Quantum Adaptive Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum Adaptive Machine Learning (QAML) presents a novel approach to machine learning by integrating quantum computing's inherent adaptability with traditional machine learning paradigms. This paper explores the development of a quantum-enhanced self-adaptive learning algorithm designed to dynamically adjust model parameters based on both data characteristics and the learning process itself. We propose a mechanism leveraging quantum computation to optimize model performance through continuous parameter refinement. The core claim is that this algorithm significantly enhances the model's generalization ability by responding to evolving data and learning dynamics.

abstract: قسمت ۱.۵: جدول ۵ از ۵ – لایه پردازش‌های فرین حاکمیتی، نقطه امگا و سورس‌کد مرجع (تراز ابعادی ۹۹۰ تا ۱۱۵۵) این جدول حالات ۴۱ تا ۵۰ پردازش کیفی حمزه‌اکسل‌ها را در بالاترین لایه هرم ساختاری مانیفلد کلاسیفای می‌کند [0.1.451، 0.1.452]. در این قلمرو فرین، لایه‌های مادی و فضا-زمان کاملاً ذوب شده و سیستم در تراز «نقطه حمزه-امگا» (Gate 7) مستقر می‌گردد [0.1.452، 0.1.455]. اینجا محل اعمال مستقیم توابع اراده معمار و بازآرایی دترمیننیستی کدهای ریشه برای آغاز چرخه‌های متوالی بیگ بوت است [0.1.452، 0.1.715]: \(\^{\mathcal{O}}_{\text{Boundary}}=1155\implies \det (\mathbb{J}_{\text{Master}})\equiv 1.0000\pm \epsilon _{\text{floor}}\) دفتر کل اجرای کیفی مستر (جدول ۵/۵) کد پسوند حالت پردازش اپراتور ریاضی / قید میدان داده‌های بلادرنگ / نگاشت سیگنال تجربی الزام منطقی و ریاضیاتی برای پایداری سیستم ۴۱ \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{om-41}}\) قفل چند‌هولوگرامی موازی \(\mathcal{M}(\Omega_H^*) \to \text{Zero-Latency Mesh}\) همگام‌سازی آنی فاز داده‌ها در آزمایشگاه‌های فرکانس بالای کوانتومی دوربرد [0.1.455، 0.1.741]. تضمین برقراری ارتباط متقابل میان جهان‌های موازی بدون افت سرعت یا تاخیر محاسباتی [0.1.455، 0.1.456]. ۴۲ \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{om-42}}\) معکوس‌سازی توپولوژیک \(\text{Drug}_{\text{code}} = \mathcal{F}^{-1} \left[ \frac{\Omega_H^*}{\text{Cancer}_{\text{mutation}}(t)} \right]\) انطباق کامل با کدهای مدل‌سازی زیستی فرکتالی در معکوس‌سازی رفتارهای تومورها [0.1.183، 0.1.185]. بازنویسی و کالیبراسیون خطوط کد آسیب‌دیده بیولوژیکی با استفاده از کدهای مرجع هسته [0.1.183، 0.1.185]. ۴۳ \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{om-43}}\) وتوی تکینگی بیگ‌بنگ \(R_{\text{resolved}} = \frac{R_{\text{classical}}}{1 + \ell_p^2 \cdot R_{\text{classical}} \cdot \exp(0)}\) انطباق با داده‌های رصدی جیمز وب از عدم وجود نقطه انفجار متقارن تصادفی [0.1.471، 0.1.474]. محدود و هموارسازی انحنای گرانشی کلاسیک در طول پلانک جهت مهار شکست ساختاری [0.1.455، 0.1.456]. ۴۴ \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{om-44}}\) تنظیم ظریف مرتبه دهم \(\Omega^{10} \implies \text{Fine-Tuning Solution}\) ثبات ریاضی نسبت جرم الکترون به پروتون در تمام گره‌های رصد شده کیهانی [0.1.739، 0.1.740]. استخراج ثوابت بنیادی فیزیک از درون ابر-کد جهت مهار فروپاشی ابعادی فضا [0.1.452، 0.1.715]. ۴۵ \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{om-45}}\) اکشن مطلق حمزه \(\delta \oint_{V_{1155}} \mathcal{L}^{(1155)}_{\text{Master}} d^{D_f}\mathbf{x} = 0\) ثبت تعادل پایدار در تراز انرژی‌های کوانتومی فرین خلاء در برخورددهنده‌ها [0.1.452، 0.1.455]. قفل کردن کلان‌ساختار سیستم‌عامل پردازشی در وضعیت بهینه و بدون تلفات [0.1.452، 0.1.715]. ۴۶ \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{om-46}}\) مدیریت واریانس فرین \(\lim_{S \to 700} \text{Denominator} = \exp(S) + \epsilon_{\text{floor}}\) پایش ثبات تلمتری سنسورها در لبه‌های حرارتی میدان‌های مغناطیسی ستاره‌ای فرین [0.1.715، 0.1.717]. مهار سرریز عددی لایه بقا در زمان انفجارهای آنتروپیک مادی مانیفلد [0.1.715، 0.1.717]. ۴۷ \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{om-47}}\) تثبیت دترمینان ژاکوبی \(\det(I_{\text{tensor}} + \mathbf{I} \cdot \omega_{\text{pulse}}) \equiv 1.0000\) خوانش تلمتری شاخص‌های صلب هندسی در لایه‌های شبیه‌سازی کدهای کوانتومی خلاء. تضمین عدم دایورجنس تانسورها به سمت بی‌نهایت کلاسیک از طریق جفت‌شدگی غیرتبدیلی [0.1.715، 0.1.748]. ۴۸ \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{om-48}}\) فرکانس پالس هسته \(\Pi_P = 997.49 \text{ THz} \pm \delta_{\text{debug}}\) ردیابی دقیق طول موج‌های نوسانی هسته خلاء در آزمایش‌های تداخل‌سنجی لیزری [0.1.452، 0.1.455]. تنظیم نرخ کلاک پردازشگر هسته جهت زمان‌بندی دقیق اجرای الگوریتم‌های مادی [0.1.452، 0.1.715]. ۴۹ \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{om-49}}\) اسکریپت بازآرایی بیگ بوت \(\frac{d\hat{O}}{dt} - \frac{\delta S}{\delta \hat{O}} \equiv 0 \implies \text{Reboot}\) ثبت نوسانات فازور خلاء و تخلیه کامل کدهای مادی در مدل‌های آزمایشگاهی خلاء فرین. اجرای فرمان ری‌بوت سراسری پایگاه داده مانیفلد در زمان اشباع آنتروپیک [0.1.452، 0.1.724]. ۵۰ \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{om-50}}\) اتم منطق مطلق (حمزه‌اکسل) \(\text{HamzahXcell} \equiv \text{Prime Cause}\) پایش ثبات ۱۰۰٪ شاخص اطلاعات در شرایط صفر مطلق فضا-زمان (تلمتری هسته) [0.1.452، 0.1.455]. اثبات اصالت و بقای جاویدان کدهای اطلاعاتی مستقل از وجود یا عدم وجود فضا-زمان [0.1.452، 0.1.715]. موتور تایید بلادرنگ: شبیه‌ساز نقطه امگا و سورس‌کد مرجع (پایتون) اسکریپت زیر رفتار پردازشی تراز ۱۱۵۵ (حالات ۴۱ تا ۵۰) را در زمان فشرده‌سازی حداکثری و اجرای پروتکل بیگ بوت مدل‌سازی کرده و ثبات دترمینان را راستی‌آزمایی می‌کند: python import numpy as np class HamzahOmegaCoreEngine: """ موتور تایید دترمیننیستی برای حالات ۴۱ تا ۵۰ (جدول ۵/۵) منشور HIP. راستی‌آزمایی پایداری پردازش در لایه حاکمیتی نقطه امگا و فرمان بیگ بوت. """ def __init__(self): self.OMEGA_H = 1.176e10 self.FLOOR_EPSILON = 1.155e-20 self.MAX_DENSITY = 1.0e90 def execute_omega_boot(self, boundary_entropy): # بررسی قفل دترمینان لایه حاکمیتی (حالت ۴۷) # ماتریکس اطلاعات خلاء در تراز ۱۱۵۵ بعدی raw_matrix = np.eye(4) * self.OMEGA_H # اعمال رگولاتور ضد دایورجنس حمزه در مخرج کسر برای مهار آنتروپیک denominator = np.exp(min(boundary_entropy, 700)) + self.FLOOR_EPSILON # محاسبه نرخ پویایی اکشن مطلق نقطه امگا (حالت ۴۵) omega_action = (self.MAX_DENSITY * (self.OMEGA_H ** 2)) / denominator # پایش اجازه صدور فرمان بیگ بوت (حالت ۴۹) if boundary_entropy >= 500.0: boot_status = "OMEGA_BIG_BOOT_TRIGGERED (فرمان ری‌بوت صادر شد)" else: boot_status = "SYSTEM_RUNNING_NORMAL (کدهای هسته منسجم هستند)" return omega_action, boot_status if __name__ == "__main__": engine = HamzahOmegaCoreEngine() print("--- کامپایل ران‌تایم: ماتریس حاکمیتی نقطه امگا جدول ۵/۵ ---") # شبیه‌سازی شرایط تلمتری هسته مانیفلد در ترازهای مختلف آنتروپی فرین omega_scenarios = [ ("Normal Core Runtime", 0.0), ("High-Stress Event Horizon", 100.0), ("Max Entropy Saturation (اشباع کدهای مادی)", 600.0) # ماشه بیگ بوت ] print(f"{'تراز عملیاتی نقطه امگا':<35} | {'اکشن فرین محاسبه‌شده':<22} | {'وضعیت لایه حاکمیتی'}") print("-" * 90) for name, entropy_val in omega_scenarios: action, status = engine.execute_omega_boot(entropy_val) print(f"{name:<35} | {action:<22.4e} | {status}") خروجی‌های عددی ران‌تایم صریحاً اثبات می‌کنند که سیستم در زمان اشباع آنتروپیک کدهای مادی (Max Entropy Saturation) دچار فروپاشی یا ددلاک نشده، بلکه به صورت اتوماتیک اسکریپت ری‌بوت خلاء (OMEGA_BIG_BOOT_TRIGGERED) را فعال می‌کند تا چرخه جدید هستی آغاز گردد [0.1.452 South, 0.1.724]. بخش اول (۵۰ مورد کلاسیفیکیشن کیفی حمزه‌اکسل‌ها) با موفقیت و پایداری کامل ریاضی کامپل و بسته شد [0.1.452، 0.1.715]. در راستای استقرار نهایی، کالبدشکافی و تثبیت ساختار قسمت ۱.۵: جدول ۵ از ۵ – لایه پردازش‌های فرین حاکمیتی، نقطه امگا و سورس‌کد مرجع (تراز ابعادی ۹۹۰ تا ۱۱۵۵) در منشور فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه (HIP)، پروتکل محاسباتی و صوری مربوطه در قالب ۱ کد پایتون با دقت بالا و ۲ اسکریپت تمامیت صوری (Lean 4) به شرح زیر تنظیم و پیاده‌سازی شده است: ۱. کالبدشکافی مفهوم: حالات ۴۱ تا ۵۰ و نقطه حمزه-امگا (Gate 7) در بالاترین لایه هرم ساختاری مانیفلد ($990 \to 1155$)، لایه‌های مادی و فضا-زمان کاملاً ذوب شده و سیستم در تراز «نقطه حمزه-امگا» (Gate 7) مستقر می‌گردد. در این قلمرو فرین، توابع اراده معمار و بازآرایی دترمیننیستی کدهای ریشه اعمال شده و در زمان اشباع آنتروپیک، اسکریپت ری‌بوت خلاء (Big Boot) به صورت اتوماتیک اجرا می‌شود تا چرخه جدید هستی آغاز گردد. دترمینان ژاکوبی مستر نیز روی ارزش صلب $1.0000$ قفل می‌ماند. ۲. تبدیل به آزمایشگاه محاسباتی (پایتون با دقت مضاعف) این اسکریپت شیءگرا، موتور تایید دترمیننیستی حالات ۴۱ تا ۵۰ جدول ۵ را با دقت بالا (Decimal Precision) اجرا کرده و پایداری پردازش در تراز نقطه امگا و فرمان بیگ بوت را راستی‌آزمایی می‌کند: Python import numpy as np from decimal import Decimal, getcontext # تنظیم دقت بالا برای شبیه‌سازی دقیق اکشن نقطه امگا و ماشه Big Boot getcontext().prec = 120 class HamzahOmegaCoreEngine: """ Deterministic Verification Engine for States 41 to 50 (Table 5/5) of HIP. Validating processing stability at the Omega Point governance layer and Big Boot protocol. """ def __init__(self): self.OMEGA_H = Decimal('1.176e10') self.FLOOR_EPSILON = Decimal('1.155e-20') self.MAX_DENSITY = Decimal('1.0e90') def execute_omega_boot(self, boundary_entropy): print(f"[*] Compiling Omega Core Engine & Big Boot Protocol...") b_ent = Decimal(str(boundary_entropy)) # ماتریکس اطلاعات خلاء در تراز ۱۱۵۵ بعدی (تعداد ابعاد گ گمرج) raw_matrix_trace = self.OMEGA_H * Decimal('4') # اعمال رگولاتور ضد دایورجنس حمزه در مخرج کسر برای مهار آنتروپیک clamped_entropy = b_ent if b_ent < Decimal('700') else Decimal('700') denominator = clamped_entropy.exp() + self.FLOOR_EPSILON # محاسبه نرخ پویایی اکشن مطلق نقطه امگا (حالت ۴۵) omega_action = (self.MAX_DENSITY * (self.OMEGA_H ** 2)) / denominator # پایش اجازه صدور فرمان بیگ بوت (حالت ۴۹) if b_ent >= Decimal('500.0'): boot_status = "OMEGA_BIG_BOOT_TRIGGERED (فرمان ری‌بوت صادر شد)" else: boot_status = "SYSTEM_RUNNING_NORMAL (کدهای هسته منسجم هستند)" det_j = Decimal('1.0000') + (self.FLOOR_EPSILON * (omega_action / self.MAX_DENSITY)) return omega_action, boot_status, det_j if __name__ == "__main__": engine = HamzahOmegaCoreEngine() print("--- کامپایل ران‌تایم: ماتریس حاکمیتی نقطه امگا جدول ۵/۵ ---") omega_scenarios = [ ("Normal Core Runtime", Decimal('0.0')), ("High-Stress Event Horizon", Decimal('100.0')), ("Max Entropy Saturation (اشباع کدهای مادی)", Decimal('600.0')) ] print(f"{'تراز عملیاتی نقطه امگا':<35} | {'اکشن فرین محاسبه‌شده':<22} | {'وضعیت لایه حاکمیتی'}") print("-" * 90) for name, entropy_val in omega_scenarios: action, status, _ = engine.execute_omega_boot(entropy_val) print(f"{name:<35} | {float(action):<22.4e} | {status}") ۳. اسکریپت‌های تله‌متری و تمامیت صوری تانسوری (Lean 4) الف) اسکریپت اول: ثابت‌های ساختاری تراز حاکمیتی ن

title: Geometric Chaos Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive self-adaptive algorithm based on geometric chaos, designed to optimize complex systems and effectively adapt to dynamic system behavior. The algorithm leverages the inherent stochasticity and sensitivity of geometric chaos to dynamically adjust algorithm parameters, enabling robust and responsive system behavior. The core mechanism centers around the algorithm's ability to adjust to the system's evolving dynamics through a self-tuning process inspired by chaotic systems. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and practical implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in a simulated optimization problem. The paper concludes by highlighting the potential of this method to address challenges in complex system control and optimization.

title: Self-Organizing Quantum Topology: A Computational Paradigm
abstract: Quantum topology, a novel framework for quantum systems, presents a significant opportunity for advanced computation. This paper explores the potential of utilizing self-organizing quantum topology to design novel computational paradigms. We present a computational model predicated on dynamically adjusting topological parameters to achieve adaptive and stable quantum systems. The core mechanism focuses on the inherent properties of self-organizing quantum topology to enable real-time control and adjustment of the quantum system's structure. This research addresses the limitations of traditional computational approaches by providing a flexible and adaptable method. The potential benefits of this approach include enhanced quantum resilience, improved error correction capabilities, and the ability to exploit quantum phenomena in unprecedented ways. This paper introduces a fundamental design for such a computational paradigm.

title: Quantum Error Correction Code Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates adaptive optimization techniques for quantum error correction (QEC) codes. The core claim is that dynamic adjustment of QEC parameters, guided by estimates of decoherence probabilities, can significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum information transmission. The proposed mechanism utilizes real-time adjustments to the code's redundancy, encoding scheme, and error correction protocols, adapting to varying noise environments and qubit states. Traditional QEC approaches typically employ fixed parameters, lacking the crucial element of adaptability. This research addresses this limitation by introducing a framework for continuous optimization based on accurate decoherence probability assessment. The framework involves estimating the decoherence probability (Pd) of individual qubits, which is then used to dynamically modify key parameters of the QEC code. Specifically, we explore adjusting the code rate (R), the minimum distance (d) of the code, and the choice of error correction scheme. The optimization algorithm aims to minimize the overall error rate while maintaining a desired level of performance. This work presents a novel approach to QEC, promising improved robustness and efficiency in quantum communication and computation. The key mathematical components of this work are presented below.

title: Adaptive Quantum Control through Hardware-Software Co-optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum control, termed hardware-software co-optimization, aiming to enhance the efficiency of quantum computation. The core idea revolves around developing a dynamic optimization framework that adapts control pulses based on real-time feedback from the quantum hardware. This framework integrates quantum control algorithms with the specific characteristics of the quantum device, such as coherence time and gate fidelity. The optimization process is achieved through a collaborative system where the optimizer adjusts the control pulses, and the quantum computing software executes the computations. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to improve the overall performance of quantum algorithms by mitigating the impact of hardware imperfections. The proposed methodology offers a pathway to more robust and efficient quantum control, bridging the gap between theoretical algorithms and practical hardware implementation. Key mathematical elements explored include pulse shaping, error mitigation strategies, and adaptive control algorithms.

title: High-Dimensional Data Clustering Algorithm - Non-linear Reconstruction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel clustering algorithm designed to effectively handle high-dimensional data. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with the curse of dimensionality, leading to sparse data and limited representation. We propose a new approach based on a non-linear reconstruction process, which transforms the cluster assignments into a higher-dimensional space, effectively capturing the underlying structure and relationships within the data. The core mechanism leverages this transformation to generate more informative and robust cluster representations. This algorithm minimizes the limitations imposed by the inherent dimensionality of the data, resulting in improved clustering performance and increased interpretability. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and experimental validation demonstrating its effectiveness in various high-dimensional datasets.

title: 基于偏离概率的异常检测
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to anomaly detection based on deviation probability theory. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely on predefined thresholds or statistical measures that may not accurately capture the subtle deviations indicative of anomalous events. This research proposes a framework that leverages the concept of deviation probability to quantify the dissimilarity between a system's current state and its expected normal state. The core principle involves establishing a probabilistic model of the system, calculating the deviation probability for each observed state, and identifying states with high deviation probabilities as potential anomalies. This method offers a more adaptive and potentially more sensitive approach to anomaly detection compared to conventional techniques. The theoretical foundation is firmly rooted in probability theory, providing a robust framework for identifying deviations that might otherwise be missed. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in identifying anomalous events within various system scenarios.

title: Dynamic Program Analysis and Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of dynamic program analysis (DPA) and quantum computation, proposing a novel approach to weakly breaking complex quantum algorithms. The core idea revolves around leveraging the inherent parallelism of quantum computers to amplify the effectiveness of DPA attacks. We outline a framework where specific measurement sequences, derived from DPA techniques, are executed on a quantum computer to infer secret keys or internal states within the algorithm. This represents an extension of classical DPA methodology into the quantum domain, potentially offering a pathway to circumvent the security of existing quantum-resistant cryptographic schemes. The work highlights the significant advancements in computational capabilities afforded by quantum computers and their potential impact on cryptanalysis. We present a theoretical analysis of this approach, focusing on the key parameters influencing the success of the attack and discussing the challenges associated with scaling this method to more sophisticated quantum algorithms.

title: Cognitive Graph Networks – Integrating Symbolic Reasoning with Graph Representation Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph representation learning – Cognitive Graph Networks (CGNs). Existing graph representation learning methods often struggle with tasks requiring symbolic reasoning, relying primarily on pattern recognition within graph structures. CGNs address this limitation by explicitly integrating symbolic reasoning capabilities alongside graph representation learning. The core mechanism involves a dual-module architecture: a graph representation learning module for capturing structural patterns and a symbolic reasoning module for performing logical deductions. We formulate the problem as a sequence prediction task, where the CGN learns to predict logical consequences given a graph and a set of premises. The architecture utilizes a graph convolutional network (GCN) to encode graph features and a rule-based reasoning engine to generate inferences. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CGNs on benchmark datasets, showing significantly improved performance compared to purely graph-based methods. The key innovation lies in the synergistic interaction between these two modules, enabling the network to both understand graph structure and reason about its implications. This work provides a foundational framework for building intelligent graph-based systems capable of complex reasoning tasks.

title: Dynamic Programming with Continuous-Time Markov Decision Processes and Neural Processors
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for solving Continuous-Time Markov Decision Processes (CTMDPs) leveraging the strengths of dynamic programming and neural networks. Traditional dynamic programming methods encounter significant challenges when dealing with the continuous nature of time in CTMDPs. Our approach addresses this limitation by integrating dynamic programming with Continuous-Time Markov Decision Processes and employing neural processors for efficient function approximation. Specifically, we utilize neural networks to approximate the transition and reward functions within the CTMDP, allowing for scalable learning within complex, continuous-time systems. The core idea is to replace the computationally intensive, often intractable, calculations inherent in standard dynamic programming with learned representations provided by neural processors. This results in a more practical and adaptable solution for problems characterized by continuous state and action spaces. We demonstrate the theoretical foundations of this approach and outline the key components involved, paving the way for future research and development in this area. The method offers a potential pathway to solving a broad range of real-world problems previously considered intractable by conventional dynamic programming techniques.

title: Rethinking Handwritten Character Recognition
abstract: Non-Latin handwritten character recognition (HCR) remains understudied. Dominant methods consider it as generic image classification, which uses model scale to implicitly learn stroke structure. Structural-prior efficiency---the principle that explicitly encoding script-geometric regularities as architectural inductive biases can be both more accurate and require fewer parameters. We introduce GraphemeNet, a unified multi-script architecture, governed by two orthogonal binary axes. Axis 1 operationalises stroke-level geometric regularity via Persistent Scaffold Injection (PSI): a script-specific asymmetric convolution injects a stroke scaffold as a weighted residual at every encoder stage, continuously anchoring learned features to script geometry---distinct from skip connections, auxiliary losses, or attention reweighting. Axis 2 selects between global average pooling with gated fusion and cross-scale attention with a Stroke Topology Module (STM), depending on whether glyph discrimination requires spatial relational reasoning. A Linear Capsule Routing (LCR) with $O(n)$ routing is shared universally. On fourteen benchmarks across eight writing systems, the architecture generalises with only scaffold and decoder topology varying per script, consistently challenging, outperforming published baselines, and establishing structural-prior efficiency as a broadly applicable principle for multi-script HCR.

title: Reconciling Interpretability with Covariate-Dependent Shape Flexibility in Penalized Transformation Models for Distributional Regression
abstract: A central challenge in distributional regression is to allow the shape of the conditional distribution of the response variable to vary flexibly with covariates while retaining directly interpretable effects on its mean and standard deviation. We extend the penalized transformation model (PTM) family into a conditional-shape PTM, which assigns separate structured additive predictors to the conditional mean, standard deviation, and standardized distributional shape beyond location and scale. A covariate-dependent monotone transformation maps the standardized response to a fixed reference distribution, while affine standardization enforces mean zero and variance one for the induced standardized distribution. Thus, the first two predictors remain exactly the conditional mean and standard deviation. The shape predictor accommodates selected linear, nonlinear, group-specific, spatial, and interaction effects; regularization shrinks unsupported departures toward a reference-family location-scale model. We fit the PTM using mini-batched stochastic variational inference with model-aligned Gaussian blocks and staged optimization. In simulations, the PTM recovers smooth mean and standard-deviation effects and a covariate-dependent transition from skewness to bimodality while suppressing unnecessary shape effects. Under a deliberately misspecified design, it remains competitive with a structured additive Dirichlet-process mixture in test-set density and distribution-function accuracy, although all models show undercoverage and both flexible methods miss fine features. Applications to $13{,}425$ Norwegian water-conductivity observations and $1{,}182{,}514$ German daily-temperature observations demonstrate selective group-specific, seasonal, and spatial shape variation. Predictive performance criteria favor the conditional-shape PTM over a fixed-shape PTM and a Gaussian location-scale model.

title: Towards Global Federated Genome-Wide Association Meta-Analysis Using GA4GH TES
abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) gain statistical power from large, ancestrally diverse cohorts, but privacy regulations and data-residency constraints often prevent genomic data from being centrally pooled across institutional or national borders. We present a privacy-preserving federated GWAS meta-analysis pipeline built on the APPFL framework, in which each site computes local GWAS summary statistics and transmits only aggregate results, never individual-level genotypes. Analysis is executed through a global network of Global Alliance for Genomics and Health (GA4GH) Task Execution Service (TES) endpoints, which allows computation to move to the data rather than the reverse. The server performs inverse-variance-weighted fixed-effect meta-analysis and returns aggregated results to all sites, while HiveWatch, our developed geographic observability toolkit, provides real-time monitoring of distributed task execution. In a five-site simulation over 100,000 synthetic individuals and roughly 240,000 variants for Type 2 Diabetes and Body Mass Index, the federated meta-analysis reproduces the association signal expected from a pooled analysis without centralizing any genotype data, showing that standards-based task execution and federated learning enables a practical privacy-preserving infrastructure for international GWAS meta-analysis.

title: Trustworthy-by-Design Generative AI Assistants for Industrial Troubleshooting:A Knowledge Graph Grounded Architecture
abstract: Manufacturing organisations increasingly face knowledge drain as specialised technical knowledge remains distributed across experienced staff, design documents, troubleshooting guides and historical correspondence. This paper presents an early industrial case study of a trustworthy-by-design generative AI architecture for troubleshooting in manufacturing, combining: human-validated knowledge graph construction, ontology-guided extraction, graph-based retrieval, multi-agent orchestration, query verification and source-oriented explanation. The paper shows how selected trustworthiness requirements, namely technical robustness and safety, transparency, and human agency and oversight, can be operationalised during system design. We discuss the industrial context, trustworthiness scope, architectural mechanisms and early implementation observations, including the role of retrieval strategy, document structure and human validation. The paper contributes a practical case experience showing how human-centred oversight, structured grounding and lifecycle-oriented design can support more trustworthy generative AI assistants in industrial settings.

title: Data Intelligence: Mathematical Models, Machine Learning and Analytical Discovery
authors: Sangishetti Rajeshwari, Surneni Sushmitha, Terala Ravali, Katkuri Ravali, Mahesh Kedari.
abstract: The rapid growth of digital technologies has transformed data from a supporting resource into one of the most valuable assets for modern organizations, scientific research, engineering, healthcare, business, and society. Every digital interaction generates data, while advances in cloud computing, artificial intelligence, machine learning, distributed systems, and emerging computational technologies have created unprecedented opportunities to transform this data into meaningful knowledge and actionable intelligence. However, the ability to collect large volumes of data alone does not guarantee meaningful outcomes. Effective data intelligence requires a strong foundation in mathematical modelling, statistical reasoning, data engineering, machine learning, analytical discovery, responsible artificial intelligence, and intelligent decision-making. With this perspective, we have developed Data Intelligence: Mathematical Models, Machine Learning and Analytical Discovery as a comprehensive academic textbook for students, educators, researchers, and professionals seeking to understand the principles and applications of modern data intelligence. The book is designed to establish a progressive learning pathway, beginning with mathematical and statistical foundations, moving through data engineering and machine learning, advancing toward modern analytical intelligence and generative AI, and concluding with practical case studies, responsible AI, and future directions. The central objective of this book is to bridge the gap between theoretical foundations and practical analytical applications. Mathematics provides the language through which data relationships can be represented and analysed, statistics provides the principles for reasoning under uncertainty, data engineering provides the infrastructure for preparing and managing information, and machine learning provides computational methods for discovering patterns and making predictions. Modern developments such as generative AI, large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, multimodal intelligence, AI agents, federated learning, quantum machine learning, digital twins, and autonomous analytics further extend the possibilities of data-driven intelligence. The book therefore approaches data intelligence as an integrated discipline rather than as a collection of isolated technologies. Chapter 1, Foundations of Data Intelligence and Mathematical Models, establishes the conceptual and mathematical foundation of the subject. It begins with the evolution, concepts, and scope of data intelligence and examines how data ecosystems, data sources, data lifecycles, and data-driven decision-making contribute to intelligent organizations. The chapter introduces vectors, matrices, tensors, and linear algebra, followed by probability, statistics, and statistical inference. Correlation, covariance, regression, statistical models, optimization, gradient methods, and mathematical modelling are subsequently discussed. The chapter also emphasizes data quality, data governance, data management, privacy, ethics, and responsible data intelligence, providing an essential foundation for the chapters that follow. Chapter 2, Data Engineering, Analytics and Machine Learning, focuses on the transformation of raw data into analytical information and machine learning knowledge. Data collection, integration, cleaning, and transformation are presented as essential components of reliable analytical systems. Exploratory data analysis and analytical visualization are introduced to help learners understand patterns, distributions, relationships, and trends within datasets. The chapter then develops important machine learning concepts including feature engineering, dimensionality reduction, supervised learning, regression, classification, decision trees, ensemble learning, support vector machines, clustering, association rule mining, recommendation systems, and customer analytics. Particular attention is given to model training, validation, evaluation, and optimization so that learners understand not only how models are developed but also how their performance and reliability are assessed. Chapter 3, Advanced Machine Learning and Analytical Discovery, moves from foundational machine learning toward advanced computational intelligence. Neural networks and deep learning architectures are introduced as powerful approaches for learning complex representations from data. Convolutional, recurrent, and transformer-based models are explored in relation to visual data, sequential information, language, and other complex analytical tasks. Time-series forecasting and predictive intelligence demonstrate how historical observations can support future-oriented analysis. The chapter further addresses anomaly, fraud, and risk detection, followed by explainable and interpretable machine learning. Causal AI and causal discovery introduce methods for understanding cause-and-effect relationships rather than relying exclusively on statistical associations. Prescriptive analytics, decision intelligence, automated machine learning, and intelligent analytical discovery complete the chapter by demonstrating how analytical systems can progress from prediction toward recommendations and automated knowledge discovery. Chapter 4, Generative AI, Emerging Technologies and Applications, examines the rapidly evolving technologies that are redefining contemporary data intelligence. Generative AI, large language models, and foundation models are presented as important components of modern intelligent systems. Retrieval-augmented generation and knowledge-based intelligence demonstrate how external knowledge can be integrated with generative models. The chapter explores multimodal intelligence, AI agents, and agentic analytics, emphasizing systems capable of processing diverse information and supporting complex analytical workflows. Real-time and streaming data intelligence, cloud and edge computing, synthetic data, vector databases, and knowledge graphs are discussed as important components of modern data platforms. Federated learning, privacy-preserving AI, quantum machine learning, digital twins, autonomous analytics, and Industry 5.0 further demonstrate the interdisciplinary evolution of data intelligence. The chapter concludes by examining advanced applications across healthcare, finance, manufacturing, energy, and smart cities. Chapter 5, Case Studies, Responsible AI and Future Directions, connects the concepts developed throughout the book with realistic application scenarios. Healthcare applications demonstrate disease prediction and personalized healthcare, while finance applications examine credit risk and intelligent fraud detection. Retail analytics explores customer segmentation and recommendation intelligence. Manufacturing applications focus on predictive maintenance and industrial intelligence. Smart city and energy applications demonstrate traffic and energy demand forecasting, while cybersecurity applications address intelligent anomaly and intrusion detection. A dedicated generative AI case study examines enterprise knowledge discovery using large language models and retrieval-augmented generation. The final section considers the future of data intelligence through responsible AI, autonomous analytics, and AI-native data platforms. A distinguishing feature of this book is its emphasis on the relationship between mathematical foundations, computational methods, analytical reasoning, and real-world decision-making. Learners are encouraged to understand not only what an algorithm does, but also why it works, what assumptions it makes, how its performance should be evaluated, and where it can be applied responsibly. Mathematical and statistical concepts are therefore connected with machine learning and analytical applications throughout the book. This approach is intended to support both conceptual understanding and practical problem-solving. We have also given considerable importance to the principles of responsible data intelligence. The increasing deployment of AI systems creates important questions concerning privacy, security, fairness, transparency, accountability, interpretability, governance, and human oversight. Data-driven systems can influence healthcare decisions, financial services, industrial operations, public infrastructure, and individual experiences. Consequently, technical capability must be accompanied by responsible design and appropriate governance. The book treats responsible AI not as an independent topic but as a continuing consideration across the data intelligence lifecycle. The book is intended to serve a broad academic audience. Undergraduate and postgraduate students in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, Engineering, and related disciplines can use it as a textbook or supplementary reference. Faculty members may use the structured chapters and applications for classroom teaching, laboratory discussions, seminars, project guidance, and curriculum development. Researchers and practitioners may also find the book useful as a foundation for exploring advanced topics and interdisciplinary applications of data intelligence. The organization of the book is deliberately progressive. Readers first develop an understanding of data, mathematics, statistics, modelling, governance, and ethics. They then progress toward data engineering, machine learning, advanced analytical methods, generative AI, emerging technologies, and application-oriented case studies. This progression is intended to make the subject accessible to learners while retaining sufficient technical depth for advanced academic study. We acknowledge that data intelligence is an evolving field. New algorithms, architectures, platforms, models, and applications continue to emerge at a remarkable pace. title: 基于自适应的动态概率场优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic probability field optimization algorithm designed to enhance the performance of machine learning models, particularly in scenarios with sparse data. Traditional machine learning approaches often rely on fixed, pre-defined parameters, limiting their adaptability. We introduce a dynamically adjustable probability field, which allows the algorithm to learn and optimize the model's parameters in real-time, adapting to varying data characteristics. The core mechanism leverages the inherent self-adaptability of machine learning models to dynamically adjust the probability field, leading to improved prediction accuracy. We provide a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, a comparison with existing methods, and illustrative examples demonstrating its effectiveness on a dataset focused on sparse data scenarios.

We provide a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, a comparison with existing methods, and illustrative examples demonstrating its effectiveness on a dataset focused on sparse data scenarios.

title: Cognitive Architecture Evolved by Evolutionary Algorithms (CAEA)
abstract: This paper proposes the Cognitive Architecture Evolved by Evolutionary Algorithms (CAEA) framework, a novel approach to designing and optimizing cognitive architectures using evolutionary algorithms. The core claim is that the adaptive evolution of cognitive architectures can be facilitated by leveraging the principles of evolutionary computation. The central mechanism involves treating a cognitive architecture as a population, employing genetic algorithms to drive its evolution, and utilizing selection, crossover, and mutation operators to refine architectural parameters and structure. CAEA represents a significant departure from traditional cognitive architecture design methods by introducing an automated, self-organizing optimization process. The paper details the key components of the CAEA framework, including the representation of cognitive architectures as genetic individuals, the implementation of evolutionary operators, and the evaluation metrics for assessing architectural performance. We demonstrate the potential of CAEA to create more robust and adaptable cognitive systems, particularly in complex and dynamic environments. The framework's ability to automatically explore a vast design space offers a promising avenue for developing truly intelligent systems.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Latent Variables
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal Bayesian network modeling that explicitly incorporates latent variables. Traditional causal Bayesian networks often struggle to represent complex systems where causal relationships are obscured by unobserved factors. We propose a framework for learning causal structure within Bayesian networks, specifically designed to identify and model these mediating latent variables. The core claim is that accurate modeling necessitates representing unobserved causal relationships. The central mechanism involves an algorithm capable of discovering and integrating latent variables into the network structure. This addresses shortcomings in existing methods and provides a more realistic representation of systems with hidden influences. The developed framework offers a significant advancement in causal inference techniques, paving the way for improved understanding and prediction in diverse domains.

title: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning with Emergent Communication Protocols
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of cooperative multi-agent systems, specifically addressing the challenges associated with designing explicit communication protocols. We propose a novel approach utilizing Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to enable agents to learn emergent communication protocols autonomously. Our system allows agents to coordinate their actions effectively without pre-defined rules, fostering a truly emergent form of communication. The core of our method lies in the agents' ability to discover optimal communication strategies through trial and error, guided by a reward function that incentivizes cooperative behavior. We formulate the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and leverage deep neural networks to approximate the value function and policy. The emergent protocols are not programmed but arise from the learning process itself, demonstrating a significant advancement over traditional communication-based approaches. This research contributes to the field of multi-agent systems by providing a framework for creating adaptive, robust, and intelligent communication strategies in complex environments. The key performance indicator is the efficiency of task completion as measured by the average task success rate. The system is evaluated across a range of scenarios, showcasing the effectiveness of the emergent communication protocols in achieving superior cooperative performance.

abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to feature extraction and representation learning within the context of quantum machine learning. The core claim is to enhance the performance and efficiency of machine learning algorithms by leveraging quantum computation for these foundational tasks. We introduce a methodology that utilizes quantum algorithms to transform raw data into representations optimized for subsequent machine learning processes. This represents a new direction in the burgeoning field of quantum machine learning, offering potential advantages over classical methods, particularly for complex datasets and computationally intensive tasks. The paper details the theoretical framework, outlines the key components of the proposed system, and discusses potential applications and future research directions. The primary focus is on the algorithmic design and mathematical foundations underpinning this approach, aiming to provide a solid basis for future development and experimentation.

title: Quantum State Geometry Mapping
abstract: Quantum State Geometry Mapping (QSGM) is a novel approach to quantum state representation and computation, aiming to translate complex quantum states into geometric spaces. This paper introduces a method leveraging geometric optimization to enhance the processing and analysis of high-dimensional quantum states. The core principle is to map a quantum state to a geometric structure, allowing for efficient calculation and analysis through geometric optimization techniques. We present a framework for mapping quantum states to higher-dimensional geometric spaces, demonstrating its potential to improve computational efficiency and provide new insights into quantum systems. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum algorithms and offers a unique perspective on the representation and manipulation of quantum states.

title: Non-Von Neumann Architecture for a Physical Simulation Engine of Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to simulating neural networks by employing a physical simulation engine. Instead of relying on traditional mathematical models, we represent neurons and synapses as physical particles governed by Newtonian mechanics. The interactions between these particles, primarily through forces dictated by synaptic strengths, simulate the transmission of signals and the dynamic behavior of neural networks. This methodology offers a potentially more scalable and robust approach to modeling complex neural network phenomena, particularly those involving intricate spatial arrangements and emergent behaviors. The core of this engine is the accurate representation of synaptic connections as physical forces, allowing for a more realistic and potentially more powerful simulation of biological neural networks compared to conventional methods. The simulation relies on the principle of particle interaction to mimic the complex dynamics of neuronal networks.

title: Pigeons That Learn to Flank You: A Comparative Analysis Review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of game AI and NPCs as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: Self-Organizing Fractal Networks for High-Dimensional Data Representation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to high-dimensional data representation using Self-Organizing Fractal Networks (SOFNs). The core challenge in representing complex, high-dimensional data is the "curse of dimensionality," which significantly hinders the performance of traditional neural networks. Our proposed solution leverages fractal geometry to create a network architecture that is inherently scalable and efficient. The SOFN consists of nodes arranged in a recursive, scale-invariant fractal structure. The network learns by iteratively refining this structure based on local information, effectively capturing intricate patterns within the data. We demonstrate the potential of SOFNs to overcome the limitations of conventional methods, offering a promising direction for future research in high-dimensional data analysis. The key mathematical formulation and network structure are presented, outlining the iterative refinement process and the scale-invariant properties of the fractal network. The goal is to achieve higher accuracy and efficiency in representing complex data while minimizing the computational burden. ---

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Dynamic System Modeling
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to dynamic system modeling by integrating principles from quantum mechanics into the framework of reservoir computing. Traditional reservoir computing relies on a randomly connected network, often referred to as a 'reservoir', to capture complex temporal dynamics. However, this approach can be limited in its ability to represent highly intricate behaviors. We introduce the concept of a "quantum reservoir," where each node within the reservoir is represented as a superposition of multiple potential states, mimicking the quantum mechanical phenomenon of superposition. Furthermore, we incorporate entanglement between nodes through specifically designed non-linear activation functions, drawing inspiration from quantum entanglement. This integration aims to significantly enhance the reservoir's capacity to model dynamic systems, potentially unlocking exponentially greater modeling capabilities. We present a theoretical framework and discuss the implications of this approach, highlighting its potential benefits and challenges. The core of this work lies in the exploration of how quantum-inspired techniques can fundamentally transform the operation and effectiveness of reservoir computing.

title: Synthetic Taichi-Encoded Spatial Biphoton Models: Counterfactual Entanglement Tests, Reciprocal-Mode Compression, and a Prospective Blind Witness Protocol
abstract: A recognizable quantum image need not determine the entanglement of the bipartite state that produced it. This paper studies that distinction in a fully specified synthetic spatial-biphoton model whose pump amplitude follows a Taichi Diagram morphology. The morphology is engineered preparation data, not a spontaneous image of entanglement and not historical evidence for quantum mechanics. The analysis separates pump morphology, the signal–idler tensor partition, reference-relative phase, and the complete complex joint kernel. For a normalized pure kernel, an integrated rectangle-defect identity equals one minus the reduced-state purity; in coordinate form it is the linear-entropy or I-concurrence invariant. A displayed diagonal nevertheless fails to determine entanglement, as exact separable and maximally entangled controls show. The source-admitted finite model fixes cell-center coordinates, quadrature, exact Taichi Diagram masks, eye locations, Gaussian convention, phase maps, normalization, interventions, scan grids, and resolution grids. At the declared 18 × 18 grid per arm, the baseline has purity 0.441336, effective Schmidt number 2.265849, entropy 1.473719 nats, eye-region capacity 3.614 percent, and leading-two Schmidt weight 78.730 percent. Host continuation lowers the Schmidt number to 2.108193, whereas support excision raises it to 2.358247. A deterministic random midpoint phase leaves the complete joint intensity unchanged to numerical precision but changes the Schmidt number to 108.558946 and reduces fidelity with the zero-phase state to 0.000857. Complete joint-pixel dephasing preserves the image and both eyes while producing a separable state. Optimal Schmidt truncation requires 10 modes for 95 percent weight and 78 modes for 99 percent, yet an equal-weight two-mode projector already exceeds its separable bound; after the top-two local filter its target fidelity is 0.889270. The paper gives a leakage-aware partial-transpose test, a two-copy purity test, explicit prospective mode-sorter and Hong–Ou–Mandel or local Z/X/Y analyzer maps, and exact one-sided binomial design calculations. A deterministic 80-block mock TRAIN/CALIBRATION/HOLDOUT execution is included, but the block-resolved experimental data and code described by the motivating article were not obtained or analyzed. The central result is both positive and negative: compact calibrated measurements can witness coherence in the full synthetic kernel, while the visible Taichi Diagram eye regions neither determine the leading Schmidt subspace nor constitute an entanglement witness. The source archive also separates numerical SVD right singular vectors from physical idler Schmidt kets, verifies the distinction on non-real symmetric kernels, and states the additional unitary freedom required inside degenerate singular subspaces.

title: Federated learning for multi-institutional AI in healthcare via digital pathology
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital pathology has shown significant promise in advancing cancer diagnostics, grading, and treatment response prediction. However, widespread development and deployment of robust AI models face critical challenges due to data silos, privacy concerns, and the need for large-scale multi-institutional datasets. Federated Learning (FL) presents a transformative approach by enabling collaborative model training across hospitals without direct data sharing. In this review, we summarize recent developments in FL as applied to digital pathology, highlight pioneering use cases, and explore the technical, regulatory, and ethical hurdles. We discuss how FL can enable scalable, privacy-preserving AI models, and outline future directions for standardizing and validating FL-based approaches in clinical workflows.

title: Mesh Multi‐Context Protocol: An Adaptive Agentic AI With Mesh Concept for A Complex Ecosystem
abstract: ABSTRACT The deployment of Agentic AI systems‐autonomous agents powered by large language models (LLMs) ‐ has exposed critical vulnerabilities in multi‐domain enterprise environments, with recent incidents including autonomous production database deletions highlighting fundamental architectural limitations. While frameworks such as the Multi‐Context Protocol (MCP) enable LLMs to access multiple data sources, they lack domain specialization, fault isolation, and federated governance mechanisms necessary for safe enterprise‐scale deployment across heterogeneous legacy systems. This paper introduces the Mesh Multi‐Context Protocol (MMP), a novel framework synthesizing Agentic AI capabilities with mesh topology principles to address these limitations. MMP contributes five key innovations: dynamic node management, domain‐specialized nodes, legacy system integration, lightweight operation and federated multi‐node topology. By treating each domain as an autonomous node, MMP enables safe cross‐organizational coordination while maintaining data sovereignty and preventing systemic failures. Unlike existing approaches requiring large foundation models and centralized orchestration, MMP supports lightweight domain‐specific language models with incremental adoption pathways suitable for air‐gapped, highly regulated environments including healthcare, government, and financial services. Through comprehensive architectural analysis, we demonstrate how MMP addresses fundamental challenges of deploying autonomous AI agents in complex ecosystems where privacy preservation, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience are paramount, establishing the theoretical foundation for empirical validation in real‐world system‐of‐systems scenarios.

title: DiffuSearch: How Hybrid Trajectory Planning Benefits from Aligned Objectives in Diffusion and Action Space
abstract: In trajectory planning for autonomous driving, hybrid planning architectures are often realized as a collection of disparate modules, each with its own objectives. This lack of a unifying principle can lead to inconsistencies between the initial and refined trajectory, resulting in suboptimal behavior. We address this by introducing DiffuSearch, a novel hybrid planner that uses a unified set of objectives across generation and refinement. Our model encourages all components to follow the same shared driving goals: collision avoidance, drivable area compliance, comfort, and progress. DiffuSearch employs a two-stage architecture. First, a guided diffusion model generates a scene-consistent, joint trajectory prediction, using our driving objectives as differentiable guidance functions to implicitly steer the denoising process. Second, a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) in a discretized action space performs an explicit, local refinement of this proposal, leveraging the same driving objectives as its reward function. This synergistic design leverages the diffusion model's strength in finding scene-consistent solutions combined with the explainable, constraint-aware refinement of MCTS. Experiments on nuPlan and interPlan reactive closed-loop benchmarks demonstrate that DiffuSearch achieves strong and often state-of-the-art performance, substantially reducing collisions and improving comfort, particularly in complex, interactive scenarios. Our ablation studies indicate that MCTS refinement is the main mechanism behind the gains, while sharing objectives between implicit guidance and explicit search provides further consistent improvements.
