title: Detecting Object Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models via Cross-Modal Attention Drifts and Mask-Based Verification
abstract: Despite recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs), object hallucination remains a major barrier to their reliable deployment. Existing detection methods often characterize visual grounding using attention from individual layers, leaving its evolution across layers underexplored. We propose CADMP, a lightweight object hallucination detection framework that combines adjacent-layer cross-modal attention drift with prediction sensitivity to targeted visual masking. During decoding, CADMP quantifies distributional changes between consecutive cross-modal attention maps to capture abrupt transitions in visual grounding. It then selects the transition with the largest drift, locates the corresponding visually relevant regions, and measures the change in prediction probability after masking these regions. These two signals provide complementary evidence: attention drift characterizes the stability of internal visual grounding, while probability variation verifies whether a prediction truly depends on the identified visual evidence. A lightweight detector integrates both signals to identify hallucinated predictions. Experiments on multiple benchmarks and representative open-source LVLMs demonstrate that CADMP achieves consistently competitive detection performance. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary contributions of adjacent-layer drift modeling and mask-based grounding verification.

title: Research on a Teaching Improvement Model for Higher Vocational Midwifery Education Integrating AI Assessment and Classroom Interaction Analysis
abstract: This study proposes a teaching-improvement model for midwifery education in higher vocational colleges that integrates artificial-intelligence-based assessment with classroom interaction analysis. The model is intended to enhance teaching quality and students’ learning experience by using AI techniques to capture dynamic information that is difficult to obtain through conventional end-of-course assessment. A dual-path architecture combining ELMo-BiLSTM-CRF with a Transformer encoder is employed to analyze classroom interaction data across multiple modalities, including speech, text, and behavioral information, thereby supporting emotion recognition, engagement assessment, and feedback on instructional strategies. The study further incorporates a closed-loop mechanism in which AI-generated assessment results are linked to instructional adjustment so that classroom interaction, learner affect, and teaching decisions can be analyzed within a unified framework. The experimental sections report model-performance analyses, group comparisons, and multimodal visualization results. In classroom interaction emotion recognition, the proposed dual-path model achieved an accuracy of 89.7%, a recall of 90.3%, and an F1 score of 90.0%, outperforming the comparative approaches reported in the study. Classroom engagement in the AI-enhanced group reached 85.9%, compared with 68.4% in the control group, while the Emotion Improvement Index increased from 0.21 to 0.43. Additional analyses illustrate how the framework can capture changes in learner emotion and engagement, examine the influence of regulatory mechanisms, and extract information relevant to teaching improvement. Overall, the results support the potential of AI-assisted classroom analytics as a decision-support tool for data-informed improvement in vocational midwifery education.

title: WP-058 — Real-Time Streaming Response Architecture: Collapsing Latency in Conversational AI Through Anticipatory Composition
abstract: Real-time streaming response differs fundamentally from classical turn-taking dialogue: the system begins composing replies before the user finishes speaking, using phonemic and syntactic cues to anticipate intent and start emitting answers mid-utterance. This paper documents the architectural shift required to support such responsiveness—lattice-threaded I/O buffering, predictive token pre-staging, and phase-locked handshake synchronisation at 132 Hz. We measure actual latency collapse (from 12+ seconds to sub-one-second) and examine the E8 geometric constraints that make this possible without sacrificing coherence integrity.

title: Probability Geometric Optimization for Quantum Computing Resource Utilization
abstract: This paper explores the application of probability geometry to optimize resource utilization within quantum computing systems. The core claim is that a novel probability geometric algorithm can significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum computations by dynamically adjusting resource allocation based on probabilistic outcomes. We present a framework that leverages the principles of probability space exploration to identify and mitigate potential bottlenecks in quantum algorithm execution. The research demonstrates the potential for substantial gains in computational speed and reduced error rates through this approach, offering a fundamentally different perspective on resource management within quantum computing. The study will analyze the algorithm's performance across a range of quantum computing tasks, comparing it to traditional optimization techniques.

title: High-Order Quantum Computing Adaptive State Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for adaptive quantum state generation in high-order quantum computing. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on pre-calculated states, limiting their flexibility and efficiency. Our proposed approach dynamically generates new quantum states based on input data and target states, significantly improving the exploration and optimization capabilities of quantum systems. The core mechanism leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum states to create a more efficient and versatile quantum computation. This advancement addresses a key limitation of existing quantum algorithms, offering a promising path towards enhanced quantum performance. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance, demonstrating its potential to unlock new quantum computational possibilities.

title: Cognitive Graph Neural Networks for Abstract Reasoning
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of Cognitive Graph Neural Networks (CGNNs) to enhance abstract reasoning capabilities. Traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) primarily focus on learning structural relationships within graph data, often lacking the ability to incorporate higher-level cognitive constraints. This research proposes a novel framework where a knowledge graph, such as Wikidata, is directly integrated into the GNN architecture, effectively embedding symbolic knowledge into the learning process. The core claim is that augmenting GNNs with cognitive constraints, represented as a symbolic graph, enables more sophisticated abstract reasoning. The proposed method leverages the relational properties inherent in knowledge graphs to guide the GNN's learning, allowing it to identify and exploit logical connections beyond purely geometric or topological features. We introduce a novel architecture and demonstrate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining a pathway towards GNNs capable of genuine abstract thought. The primary contribution lies in the integration of symbolic knowledge and graph-based learning for advanced reasoning tasks.

title: 基于量子力学原理的密码分析与防御
abstract: This paper explores novel cryptographic analysis and defense strategies rooted in the principles of quantum mechanics. It investigates vulnerabilities in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and leverages quantum decoherence to attack traditional cryptographic algorithms. The core claim is to design new cryptographic analysis methods utilizing superposition, entanglement, and decoherence. The proposed mechanisms aim to exploit inherent weaknesses within existing cryptographic systems by applying fundamental quantum phenomena. This research represents a significant departure from classical approaches, offering a potentially disruptive pathway for future cryptographic security. The analysis focuses on the theoretical aspects of these attacks and defenses, providing a framework for further investigation and development. The primary contribution lies in the conceptual integration of quantum mechanics into the field of cryptography, moving beyond purely mathematical approaches.

title: Title: Self-Referential Modular Arithmetic for Cryptography
abstract: This paper explores the application of self-referential modular arithmetic as a novel approach to enhance the security of cryptographic algorithms. Traditional cryptographic systems rely on the difficulty of solving problems involving modular arithmetic, while this work proposes a system where operations inherently reference themselves, potentially creating a self-checking loop. We introduce a new modular arithmetic system based on this principle, analyzing its potential to disrupt existing cryptosystems and offering enhanced security through its self-referential nature. The core mechanism involves the integration of self-reference into the arithmetic operations, creating a loop that is difficult to reverse without compromising the system's integrity. This paper will detail the design and analysis of this system, exploring its potential vulnerabilities and strengths.

title: Non-Linear Self-Organizing Neural Networks: A Dynamic Topology Approach
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel Non-Linear Self-Organizing Neural Network (NLSON) architecture, leveraging dynamic topology adjustment to enhance model training efficiency and performance. Traditional neural network architectures often rely on fixed, static structures, limiting their adaptability to evolving data distributions. Our proposed method introduces a dynamic topology algorithm that intelligently adjusts network structure, allowing the network to adapt to changes in data distribution. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments across a range of datasets, showcasing significant improvements in training speed and model accuracy. The core mechanism involves self-adaptive topology adjustment guided by a feedback loop, optimizing network connectivity and minimizing computational costs. This results in a more robust and adaptable model.

title: ##基于光子量子计算的通信协议优化
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of communication protocols for optical fiber networks leveraging the principles of photonic quantum computing. Traditional fiber optic communication protocols rely heavily on classical communication techniques, often facing limitations in bandwidth, security, and efficiency. This research proposes a novel approach that integrates the inherent capabilities of photonic quantum computing – specifically, quantum transmission and processing – to enhance communication protocols. The core of the approach involves optimizing encoding, modulation, and decoding schemes within the fiber network, utilizing quantum properties to achieve significant improvements in data transmission rates, security against eavesdropping, and overall system performance. We explore the theoretical framework and potential implementation challenges, demonstrating the transformative potential of this hybrid approach. The proposed protocol utilizes quantum key distribution (QKD) for secure key exchange and employs quantum error correction (QEC) to mitigate the effects of noise during transmission. Simulation results (presented conceptually) indicate a substantial increase in achievable data rates and a dramatically improved level of security compared to conventional protocols. ---

Traditional fiber optic communication protocols rely heavily on classical communication techniques, often facing limitations in bandwidth, security, and efficiency. This research proposes a novel approach that integrates the inherent capabilities of photonic quantum computing – specifically, quantum transmission and processing – to enhance communication protocols. The core of the approach involves optimizing encoding, modulation, and decoding schemes within the fiber network, utilizing quantum properties to achieve significant improvements in data transmission rates, security against eavesdropping, and overall system performance. We explore the theoretical framework and potential implementation challenges, demonstrating the transformative potential of this hybrid approach. The proposed protocol utilizes quantum key distribution (QKD) for secure key exchange and employs quantum error correction (QEC) to mitigate the effects of noise during transmission. Simulation results (presented conceptually) indicate a substantial increase in achievable data rates and a dramatically improved level of security compared to conventional protocols. ---

title: Biofeedback-Reinforced Learning with Neuro-Genetic Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to intelligent agent design by integrating the adaptive dynamic adjustment capabilities of biofeedback reinforcement learning (BRL) with the optimization prowess of the neuro-genetic algorithm (NGA). The core claim is to achieve highly adaptive and robust agents through this synergistic combination. The central mechanism involves utilizing neurofeedback to dynamically adjust the policy of a reinforcement learning (RL) agent, concurrently employing the NGA to evolve the policy space, thereby facilitating rapid adaptation and optimization. We demonstrate that this integration significantly enhances an agent's adaptability and learning efficiency compared to traditional BRL or NGA approaches. The proposed methodology offers a pathway towards creating intelligent systems capable of thriving in complex and changing environments. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key components and their interactions, followed by a discussion of the algorithm's design and potential applications. This work represents a significant advancement in the field of adaptive control and reinforcement learning.

title: 基于自适应量子拓扑的机器学习模型优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning framework, termed "Quantum-Aware Optimization for Machine Learning," leveraging the unique properties of quantum topology to optimize the performance of machine learning models. Traditional machine learning approaches often struggle with overfitting and limited generalization capabilities, particularly when dealing with complex datasets. This framework utilizes quantum computing to enhance model parameter optimization, potentially leading to improved generalization and robustness. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the model's structure and parameters based on quantum-induced fluctuations, effectively exploring a vast parameter space and mitigating local optima. This approach offers a paradigm shift in machine learning optimization, promising enhanced model performance and adaptability. The paper details the core mechanism, analyzes the potential benefits through theoretical considerations, and presents preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Title: Adaptive Geometric Transformation Clustering Algorithm
abstract: Adaptive geometric transformation clustering is a novel approach to clustering that dynamically adjusts the clustering criteria based on the data's inherent structure. This research explores the application of self-adaptive geometric transformations to enhance clustering performance, particularly in scenarios with complex data distributions. The core mechanism involves a system of geometric transformations that iteratively refine the cluster boundaries, leading to more precise and meaningful groupings. This paper introduces a framework for implementing this algorithm, detailing the geometric transformation process and its impact on the resulting cluster outcomes. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in a dataset simulating real-world scenarios.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Neural Networks with Adaptive Latent Variable Constraints
abstract: Standard Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) suffer from significant computational challenges when dealing with large datasets and intricate network architectures, hindering their practical application in numerous domains. This paper introduces a novel approach—Dynamic Bayesian Neural Networks (DBNNs) with Adaptive Latent Variable Constraints—designed to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to construct a DBNN structure that dynamically adjusts the constraints placed on latent variables based on observed data. This adaptive constraint learning mechanism dramatically reduces the computational burden associated with Bayesian inference while preserving the essential capabilities of BNNs. We present a comprehensive framework for DBNNs, detailing the architecture, the dynamic constraint adjustment process, and the underlying mathematical principles. The key innovation lies in the integration of DBNNs with a learning algorithm that optimizes the constraints iteratively, leading to improved scalability and accuracy in complex Bayesian modeling scenarios. The proposed method offers a promising avenue for applying Bayesian inference to large-scale problems where traditional BNNs are intractable.

title: How to Build a Controlled AI Assistant for Quantum Computing
abstract: An architectural approach in which free-form dialogue is turned into a controlled computational workflow: the lifecycle stage determines the AI's goal, the context available to it, and the set of tools it is allowed to use right now. The user describes a task in ordinary language, the assistant translates it into a structured scenario, helps gather the missing information, guides it through validation, runs it on a simulation-first basis, and explains the result. The LLM does not own the computational process: experiment state is stored separately from the dialogue, the AI tools available depend on the current lifecycle stage, and any run goes through independent validation and an execution policy.

title: Evaluating Deep Actor–Critic Methods for Path Planning of Mobile Manipulators Under Wheel–Terrain Interaction
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an effective paradigm for enabling autonomous robots to acquire navigation policies directly from interaction with complex and uncertain environments. Nevertheless, autonomous path planning for Skid-Steer Mobile Manipulators (SSMMs) remains a challenging problem because it requires the coordinated control of the non-holonomic mobile base and the manipulator while simultaneously accounting for obstacle avoidance and wheel–terrain interaction effects. This paper presents and evaluates RL-based path planning strategies for SSMMs, explicitly incorporating coupled dynamics of the mobile platform and manipulator to generate collision-free trajectories under varying terrain conditions. The proposed framework incorporates a slip-aware reward formulation that penalizes discrepancies between commanded and measured robot motion while accounting for longitudinal and lateral slip resulting from wheel–terrain interaction. The main contributions are (i) a unified RL-based framework based on actor–critic techniques for SSMM path planning, integrating the mobile base and manipulator dynamics within a coupled system representation; (ii) a physics-aware multi-objective reward formulation that incorporates wheel–terrain interaction into policy learning; and (iii) the implementation via simulation and field validation of the proposed policies under progressively complex navigation conditions and real underground mining scenarios. The framework is evaluated using four RL algorithms across multiple environments and maps from real mining scenarios, encompassing diverse navigation conditions and start-to-goal configurations. The evaluated methods include Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Soft Actor–Critic (SAC), and Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3). Experimental field results show that SAC achieves the lowest planning time, reducing the planning time by 127.3%, 24.1%, and 2.52% compared with PPO, TD3, and DDPG, respectively. SAC also achieves the shortest path, reducing the average path length by 20.32%, 8.58%, and 1.90% compared with PPO, DDPG, and TD3, respectively. Moreover, SAC generates smoother control profiles for both the mobile base and the manipulator arm, while TD3 exhibits competitive performance across several navigation metrics. The proposed framework demonstrates the potential of slip-aware RL for coordinated SSMM navigation, providing a practical foundation for improving the safety, energy efficiency, and operational autonomy of mobile manipulators exposed to complex mining environments.

title: DSLHash: Lightweight Hash Function Based on SVSC 4D Chaotic System and Dynamic Substitution Layers
abstract: Data integrity remains a critical requirement for secure communication in IoT environments. To address this challenge for resource-constrained IoT devices, lightweight cryptographic hash functions have been widely studied. However, static substitution layers in conventional hash functions might be vulnerable to advanced cryptanalysis. Dynamic substitution layers are constructed by exploring several methods such as key dependency, chaotic maps, DNA computations, and elliptic curves. Despite these efforts, existing dynamic substitution layers are not suitable for resource-efficient implementation. To achieve both enhanced security and practicality, this paper proposes a lightweight hash function based on a structure-varying self-coupled (SVSC) chaotic system and a dynamic substitution mechanism. A SVSC 4D chaotic map is first constructed using lightweight arithmetic and logical operations, including modular addition, bitwise shifts, and bitwise negation, thereby avoiding multiplication operations and enabling efficient hardware implementation. The chaotic map is then integrated with a generalized Feistel structure to construct a dynamic substitution layer, where the transformation behavior dynamically changes according to the internal chaotic state. This mechanism enhances nonlinear transformation diversity and contributes to improved diffusion characteristics. Finally, the dynamic substitution layer is incorporated into a sponge-based hash framework supporting flexible digest lengths. The results demonstrate that the proposed SVSC 4D chaotic system exhibits long cycle lengths in a 32-bit finite-precision implementation, mitigating the degradation caused by finite-precision effects and improving its suitability for practical cryptographic applications. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed methodology achieves a balanced tradeoff among security performance, hardware efficiency, and implementation complexity. Based on a 256-bit sponge state with a 192-bit capacity, DSLHash provides approximately 96-bit collision resistance, which is selected to balance security requirements and hardware resource consumption in lightweight applications.

title: No-Regret Bayesian Optimization with Finite-Library Input-Warped Kernels
abstract: Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization (GP-BO) excels at black-box optimization of costly functions, e.g., hyperparameter optimization (HPO) and multi-agent system (MAS) design. Convergence-rate guarantees exist for select methods, notably GP upper confidence bound (GP-UCB), but require a fixed kernel. Critically, the kernel encodes how input proximity affects objective value similarity. When raw coordinates poorly match this geometry - as with log-scaled hyperparameters or localized peaks - input warping can greatly improve sample efficiency, yet known GP-UCB proofs require a fixed kernel. We propose Finite-Library Input-Warped Bayesian Optimization (FLIWBO), which selects warps from a finite library of smooth input maps by any history-dependent rule. It adapts the input geometry to accelerate learning while retaining high-probability convergence guarantees under mild hypotheses, with an explicit $\sqrt(N_\varepsilon)$ library-size cost. Controlled diagnostics show that finite-library warping repairs planted geometry mismatches and identify FLIWBO failure cases. Across four repeated benchmarks - warped synthetic objectives, a confidence-fence trap, and Fashion-MNIST HPO - FLIWBO-UCB beats raw-coordinate GP-UCB under misspecified geometry, escapes traps that defeat even oracle-warp expected improvement, and recovers much of the gain from manual log scaling, while leading the tested methods that admit a matching regret guarantee. A 20-dimensional MAS design study further shows feasibility under costly noisy evaluations. Code for experiments is available: https://github.com/edvin-ketabati/bogp-paper-experiments.

title: Intuitionistic Unitary Linear Logic: A Proof-Theoretical Approach to Purely Quantum Higher-Order
abstract: Although the circuit model for quantum computation is well established, it is incapable of representing non-causal higher-order quantum processes such as the quantum switch. If several models of non-causal quantum computation have been considered in the literature, the approaches have so far only been focusing on the physicality of such processes, using matrices and other techniques from linear algebra. If these approaches are expressive, they however only provide a static and monolithic understanding of these processes. In this article, we propose a new formalism for non-causal, higher-order quantum processes. Based on a Curry-Howard interpetation, our proposal offers a computational interpretation that is both compositional and modular. In particular, we present Intuitionistic Unitary Linear Logic (IULL), a logic based on linear logic focusing on conservation of unitarity for higher order terms. We prove the coherence of IULLL, its completeness with regard to unitaries, and the admissibility of its cut rules. We finally discuss the validity of our approach by revisiting known non-causal quantum processes with IULL.

title: Messages Passed Along the Edges: A State of the Art Review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of GNN and graph learning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Title: Modular Quantum State Collapse for Complex Systems
abstract: Abstract: Existing quantum state collapse methods are brittle and require careful parameter tuning. We propose a modular approach where states collapse based on a set of pre-defined, highly optimized modules. This novel design addresses the limitations of traditional methods by offering a more robust and adaptable collapse mechanism, potentially simplifying complex quantum computations.

title: Probability Logic Geometry: A Dynamic Geometric Model Generator
abstract: This paper introduces Probability Logic Geometry (PLG), a novel algorithmic framework based on probabilistic geometric modeling. PLG leverages the inherent properties of probability distributions to construct dynamic geometric models, allowing for complex numerical computations and simulation. The core mechanism involves iterative refinement of a probabilistic graph, automatically generating and optimizing model parameters. This approach offers a flexible and adaptable methodology for modeling complex phenomena, particularly in areas requiring nuanced representation and dynamic adjustment. The development of PLG represents a significant advancement in geometric modeling, moving beyond static geometric representations towards a dynamic, probabilistic framework.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Iterative Refinement of Neural Network Weights
abstract: Quantum-enhanced iterative refinement of neural network weights is a promising approach to accelerate and improve the training process of complex models. This paper explores the application of quantum-inspired techniques to optimize neural network weights, focusing on minimizing energy and identifying key weights for improved performance. We present a novel method incorporating quantum-enhanced gradient descent and a quantum-inspired energy function to achieve faster convergence and enhanced robustness. The potential impact of this research lies in significantly improving the efficiency and effectiveness of training deep neural networks across a range of applications. The study demonstrates the efficacy of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results, showcasing its potential to revolutionize neural network training methodologies.

title: Relational Logic for Program Verification with Dynamic Typing
abstract: This paper explores the challenges and opportunities of applying relational logic to program verification within the context of dynamic typing systems. Traditional relational logic formulations often struggle to adequately represent and reason about the runtime behavior inherent in dynamically typed languages, leading to limitations in their ability to comprehensively verify program correctness. We propose a novel relational logic extension designed to bridge this gap, seamlessly integrating with dynamic typing. This extension introduces mechanisms to precisely capture and reason about dynamic data structures and runtime operations, significantly expanding the scope of what can be verified. The core of this work lies in combining the formal rigor of relational logic with the practical flexibility of dynamic typing, offering a powerful new tool for ensuring the reliability of dynamic programs. Our approach addresses key limitations of existing techniques and provides a solid foundation for advanced program verification.

The core of this work lies in combining the formal rigor of relational logic with the practical flexibility of dynamic typing, offering a powerful new tool for ensuring the reliability of dynamic programs. Our approach addresses key limitations of existing techniques and provides a solid foundation for advanced program verification.

title: Graph-Based Representation Learning for Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language processing, but they often struggle with tasks requiring deep understanding of relationships between entities within textual data. This research proposes a novel approach to enhance LLM performance by incorporating graph-based representation learning. The core idea is to construct a graph representation of the input text, where nodes represent words or phrases and edges represent semantic relationships derived from co-occurrence, dependency parsing, or other relevant measures. This graph is then integrated into the LLM architecture, allowing the model to leverage graph-based reasoning for improved understanding and performance. We hypothesize that this integration will address the limitations of current LLMs in representing and reasoning about complex relationships, leading to advancements in tasks such as question answering, knowledge graph completion, and commonsense reasoning. The methodology focuses on efficient graph construction and seamless integration, aiming for minimal disruption to the existing LLM structure while maximizing the benefits of relational reasoning. The evaluation framework will primarily rely on benchmark datasets designed to test relational understanding capabilities, assessing improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and robustness compared to traditional LLM approaches.

title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit Compilation for Variational Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) hold significant promise for solving complex problems across diverse fields. However, their practical implementation on near-term quantum devices is severely hampered by the pervasive effects of quantum noise. Traditional quantum circuit compilation techniques are largely static, failing to account for the unique noise profiles inherent in individual quantum hardware. This paper introduces a novel adaptive quantum circuit compilation framework designed to mitigate these limitations. The core concept centers around dynamically adjusting the circuit layout and gate decomposition in real-time, leveraging measurements of the quantum hardware's noise characteristics to optimize both the accuracy and circuit depth of the compiled quantum circuit. This approach represents a critical step towards unlocking the full potential of VQAs by enabling them to effectively operate within the constraints of noisy quantum computers. The framework incorporates feedback loops for continuous refinement, adapting to evolving noise conditions. The methodology is described, focusing on the key components: noise profiling, adaptive gate decomposition, and circuit re-optimization. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the adaptive approach in reducing circuit depth and improving the fidelity of VQA computations compared to static compilation methods. This work lays the foundation for robust and efficient VQA execution on future quantum hardware.

title: ##基于深度强化学习的机器人运动规划
abstract: This paper explores the application of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) for robot motion planning. Traditional robot motion planning methods often rely on hand-crafted rules and are difficult to adapt to complex and dynamic environments. DRL offers a promising alternative by allowing robots to learn optimal motion strategies directly from experience. This work presents a framework for training robots to autonomously plan their movements using DRL, focusing on enhancing both efficiency and safety. The core of the approach involves constructing a simulation environment for the robot and employing a DRL algorithm to train the robot's control policy. The performance of the trained policy is subsequently validated through extensive simulations. The key contributions lie in demonstrating the feasibility and potential of DRL for robust and adaptable robot motion planning, paving the way for autonomous robotic systems in diverse applications.

title: Quantum Non-Linear Geometry: Topological Structure and a Quantum Computation Model for Complex Nonlinear Geometry
abstract: Quantum non-linear geometry offers a novel approach to understanding and simulating complex geometrical phenomena, particularly those exhibiting non-linear properties. This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum non-linear geometry to construct a quantum computation model capable of revealing and manipulating topological structures. We explore the core mechanisms by which non-linear geometry can be leveraged, focusing on the self-similarity inherent in the field. The research aims to develop a model that directly simulates and analyzes topological geometric patterns, providing a foundation for advanced quantum algorithms. This work will highlight the significance of exploring this intersection of geometry and computation, offering a potential pathway to breakthroughs in both theoretical and practical applications of quantum information.

title: Algorithmic Randomness Generation via Quantum Tunneling Simulation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithmic randomness generation utilizing the principles of quantum tunneling simulation. Traditional pseudo-random number generators (PRNGs) are inherently susceptible to biases and vulnerabilities, often derived from deterministic algorithms. This research introduces a methodology that harnesses quantum phenomena, specifically the probability of tunneling through a potential well, to produce truly random sequences. The core mechanism involves modulating the tunneling probability based on a function directly related to the desired random value. This approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm for randomness generation, potentially overcoming the limitations imposed by classical PRNGs and providing a more robust and unbiased source of randomness. The simulation methodology is described in detail, along with a theoretical framework outlining the key mathematical operations involved. The potential advantages of this technique, particularly regarding its resistance to prediction and biases, are explored.

title: Core Claim: A Quantum Topological Network Design Method
abstract: Quantum topology is a rapidly emerging field of study that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics and topology to create novel computational architectures. This paper explores the application of quantum topology to network design, focusing on the development of self-organizing networks utilizing quantum entanglement and topological properties. We propose a novel design methodology that employs topological structure optimization to discover self-organizing patterns within the network, offering a potentially transformative approach to network functionality. The resulting network demonstrates enhanced resilience and adaptability compared to traditional network designs, representing a significant advancement in computational design.

title: Topological Space Information Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel information theory framework centered on the concept of information density within topologically structured spaces. Traditional information theory often focuses on the encoding and transmission of data, while topological space information theory emphasizes the inherent information content of systems. We propose a new method for assessing and compressing complex systems by leveraging the structural properties of topological spaces. This approach utilizes a defined information density function, informed by the space's inherent organization, to achieve efficient compression. The core mechanism involves quantifying information density through the analysis of topological relationships, providing a fundamentally different perspective on information representation and processing. This work contributes to the field of information theory by providing a new tool for understanding and managing complex data, particularly within systems exhibiting intricate topological structures.

title: Title: Geometric Proof of Concepts for Cryptography – New Cryptographic Protocols
abstract: This paper presents a novel cryptographic protocol predicated on geometric proofs, aiming to provide a fundamentally secure method for verifying the validity of digital signatures. Traditional cryptographic methods often rely on complex algebraic operations, making them vulnerable to attacks. This paper explores the application of geometric principles, specifically distances and angles, to construct a proof of authenticity and integrity, offering a potential alternative to existing cryptographic protocols. The core mechanism involves establishing a mathematical proof based on geometric transformations, enhancing security through unique properties inherent in geometric constructions. The proposed protocol demonstrates initial conceptual proof through geometric analysis, highlighting its potential advantages and challenges.

title: Where Perceptrons Meet Proof Trees: A Comparative Analysis Review of Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of neuro-symbolic and reasoning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Multi-Representation Signal Fusion for Robust RF-Based UAV Recognition via Structure-Guided Time–Frequency Modeling
abstract: RF-based UAV recognition is important for low-altitude security because it enables passive sensing from electromagnetic emissions without requiring target visibility or illumination. Compared with active sensing, passive RF sensing offers a wider observation range and is less constrained by line-of-sight conditions. Although deep-learning methods have improved RF-based UAV recognition, most existing approaches focus primarily on label prediction and do not explicitly model time–frequency structural characteristics, which limits their robustness in practical RF environments where UAV signals are often weak and may overlap with co-channel interference. This paper presents a multi-representation signal fusion (MRSF) framework for robust RF-based UAV recognition through structure-guided time–frequency modeling. MRSF represents each RF signal using an original time–frequency map, a residual-enhanced map, and a binarized structural map to capture global spectral patterns, enhanced signal structures, and connected spectral morphology. These representations are fused through a heterogeneous three-branch stem for backbone classification, and the binarized structural map further supports connected-region analysis to estimate occupied bandwidth, temporal duration, and signal period in non-cooperative scenarios where protocol-level parameters are unavailable. On the RFUAV dataset, MRSF achieves an average accuracy of 96.05% across target SNR levels from −20 to 20 dB and maintains 88.29% accuracy at −20 dB, demonstrating strong robustness under severe low-SNR conditions. These results show that, for UAV RF emissions acquired within the effective coverage of the front-end receiver, MRSF improves robust UAV recognition while providing interpretable spectrum-structure descriptors beyond class labels.

title: Learning to Track from Privileged Target Appearances
abstract: Target templates define what a visual tracker searches for, yet the templates available at inference trade off localization certainty with appearance freshness: the initial ground-truth template is exact but becomes stale, whereas recent templates better reflect the current appearance but are cropped from uncertain predictions. We quantify this bottleneck with a non-deployable oracle that supplies an exact current-frame target crop, improving AUC on LaSOT by 15.2 percentage points. This gap reveals a training-only opportunity: frame-level ground truths provide exact current- and future-frame target crops, although such crops are unavailable at deployment. We introduce Privileged Appearance Transfer for Tracking (PATT), a teacher-student training framework that transfers these privileged appearances to a deployable tracker through multi-level representation prediction. The privileged teacher observes exact target crops from past, current, and future frames, whereas the student receives only past-frame templates and learns to predict the teacher's search representations. To avoid transferring unreliable teacher signals, PATT weights this transfer by the teacher's relative localization advantage over the student and its absolute localization accuracy. After training, the teacher, latent predictor, reliability weights, and privileged crops are removed, leaving standard student-only inference. Across seven benchmarks at two model scales, PATT achieves consistent gains under both long- and short-term tracking protocols.

title: Perceptually Regularized Diffusion Model for Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Image super-resolution, which aims to reconstruct high-resolution images from their low-resolution observations, is fundamental to medical imaging, remote sensing, surveillance, microscopy, and scientific visualization. Traditional model-based methods formulate super-resolution as an inverse problem with hand-crafted regularization priors. While interpretable and theoretically grounded, they rely on fixed assumptions and require computationally intensive iterative solvers. Deep learning methods offer data-driven flexibility by learning nonlinear mappings from low- to high-resolution images, among which diffusion models have achieved particularly impressive perceptual quality. However, the standard diffusion training objective is a pixel-domain noise-prediction loss that does not explicitly enforce perceptual fidelity, which can lead to oversmoothing and loss of fine image structure. To address these limitations, we propose a perceptually regularized diffusion framework that incorporates prior knowledge through perceptual-loss-based regularization, improving training convergence and encouraging the recovery of meaningful image features. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate improved perceptual quality and competitive distortion metrics, highlighting the effectiveness of regularization for diffusion-based super resolution.

title: 对于LLM人机互交语义层面方法革新的探讨
abstract: Current large language models excel at surface-level pattern matching and fluent text generation, yet they systematically fail to capture implicit meaning—the "unspoken" semantic layer that drives genuine human understanding. This paper introduces the Jianmu Cognitive Dynamics Framework (V3.3), a mathematically grounded architecture designed to detect and model latent intent in multi-turn dialogue. Departing from the prevailing paradigm of scaling parameters and data, the framework formalizes a four-dimensional semantic representation—quantity (instantaneous emotional arousal), valence (factual anchoring), tense (topic continuity), and empty (logical connectivity)—and evolves these through continuous-field dynamics with emotional modulation, hard-constraint filtering, and convergence-based path classification. A reference Python implementation is provided. The authors argue that without addressing the semantic latent layer through principled cognitive modeling rather than brute-force scaling, the AI industry risks permanent stagnation in genuine interactive depth—producing fluent outputs that converge toward homogeneity while remaining deaf to what users truly mean.

title: Dynamic Probability Field: A Novel Modeling Approach
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Dynamic Probability Field (DPF) theory designed to model complex systems by dynamically adjusting probability field parameters in response to environmental changes. The core mechanism centers around utilizing neural networks to map environmental fluctuations to parameter adjustments, and an automated parameter adjustment process to maintain system stability. Traditional probabilistic models often fall short in handling dynamic environments, necessitating a more flexible and powerful modeling approach. This work proposes a new framework for dynamic system simulation and optimization, offering enhanced adaptability and precision compared to conventional methods.

title: Towards Controlled AQG: A Hybrid Approach Based on Verbal Valence (LVF) and First-Order Logic
abstract: This dataset supports the reproducibility of the experimental results reported in the paper "Towards Controlled Automatic Question Generation: A Hybrid Approach Based on Verbal Valence (LVF) and First-Order Logic" (WANDJI Alain Chamfort, MOUKOUOP NGUENA Ibrahim, University of Yaoundé I, Cameroon). The dataset contains four files: 1. dataset1_questions_500.csv — 495 questions automatically generated in French from 120 LVF/RALI verb entries across 15 semantic classes. Each question is described by its predicate arity (A), Bloom's Taxonomy level (B), word count (W), Complexity Score (SCQ = 0.4×A + 0.6×B), and Estimated Response Time (ERT = W×0.5 + A×B×5.0 seconds). 2. dataset2_response_times.csv — 59,400 response-time records collected from 120 students answering the 495 generated questions. Includes predicted ERT, observed response time (seconds), and correctness of the answer. 3. dataset3_expert_ratings.csv — Difficulty ratings provided by 3 pedagogical experts on a 100-question pilot corpus, used to calibrate the SCQ weighting coefficients (ω₁=0.4, ω₂=0.6). Inter-rater agreement: Cohen's κ = 0.66. 4. dataset4_lvf_verbs.csv — The 120 LVF verb entries used in generation, with their semantic class, predicate arity, and applicable Bloom levels. All data were generated with Python 3.10 (random seed = 42) and are fully reproducible. Key validation metrics: R²(ERT, mean observed time) = 0.999; R²(SCQ, mean expert rating) = 0.984.

title: Free-Space Holographic Beam Steering: A Zero-Fiber Architecture for Hyperscale Cryogenic Quantum Control
abstract: The scaling of superconducting quantum processors beyond the 10,000-qubit threshold is critically constrained by the physical and thermodynamic limits of input/output (I/O) control lines. While transitioning from RF coaxial cables to optical fibers and cryogenic InGaAs photodiodes mitigates passive heat ingress, it introduces a dense DC power routing bottleneck and localized active heat dissipation at the 4K stage. This specification details a "Zero-Fiber" architecture that severs the physical I/O tether entirely below the 50K stage. By separating high-speed temporal modulation from spatial routing, the system leverages a cryogenic Spatial Light Modulator (SLM) at 50K to dynamically beam-steer targeted free-space optical pulses through a thermally baffled vacuum gap. These pulses map via a microlens array onto highly non-linear Barium Titanate (BaTiO₃) passive transducers at the millikelvin (mK) stage. Integrated phononic bandgap shielding ensures high-fidelity qubit control without structural wiring density, active thermal loads, or acoustic decoherence. evidence.title: Free-Space Holographic Beam Steering: A Zero-Fiber Architecture for Hyperscale Cryogenic Quantum Control
evidence.abstract: The scaling of superconducting quantum processors beyond the 10,000-qubit threshold is critically constrained by the physical and thermodynamic limits of input/output (I/O) control lines. While transitioning from RF coaxial cables to optical fibers and cryogenic InGaAs photodiodes mitigates passive heat ingress, it introduces a dense DC power routing bottleneck and localized active heat dissipation at the 4K stage. This specification details a "Zero-Fiber" architecture that severs the physical I/O tether entirely below the 50K stage. By separating high-speed temporal modulation from spatial routing, the system leverages a cryogenic Spatial Light Modulator (SLM) at 50K to dynamically beam-steer targeted free-space optical pulses through a thermally baffled vacuum gap. These pulses map via a microlens array onto highly non-linear Barium Titanate (BaTiO₃) passive transducers at the millikelvin (mK) stage. Integrated phononic bandgap shielding ensures high-fidelity qubit control without structural wiring density, active thermal loads, or acoustic decoherence. title: Dynamic Graph Rewiring for Evolutionary Robotics
abstract: Evolutionary robotics provides a powerful framework for designing robots capable of solving complex tasks through automated evolution. However, a significant limitation of traditional evolutionary robotics approaches is their reliance on fixed robot morphologies. This restricts the robot's ability to adapt effectively to dynamic and unpredictable environments. This paper introduces a novel dynamic graph rewiring algorithm designed to overcome this constraint. The algorithm allows the internal connectivity of a robot's nervous system—represented as a dynamic graph—to evolve over time, enabling a more robust and adaptive evolutionary process. The core mechanism involves iteratively modifying the graph structure based on performance feedback, allowing the robot to rewire its connections and optimize its control strategy for the current task and environment. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, highlighting its advantages over static morphology-based methods. The proposed framework offers a pathway towards more adaptable and robust evolutionary robotics systems, drawing inspiration from biological neural networks.

title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Quantum State Generation
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of theoretical physics, posits that space is fundamentally discrete and that its properties can be described by topological invariants. This concept has profound implications for quantum computation, suggesting the possibility of creating robust and adaptable quantum states. This paper explores the design and implementation of an adaptive quantum state generation algorithm leveraging quantum topology principles. The core mechanism centers around the creation of 'self-adjusting' topological rules, allowing the system to dynamically modify its quantum state in response to environmental changes, ultimately enhancing the efficiency of quantum calculations and data processing. We present a conceptual framework and initial implementation using Python, focusing on the core algorithm's design and the potential for automated de-duplication. The paper will discuss the theoretical underpinnings, challenges, and potential applications of this approach.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Networks for Modeling Human Cognitive Processes
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling human cognitive processes using Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs). Traditional Bayesian Networks (BNs) often fall short in representing the inherently dynamic and evolving nature of human thought. This research proposes a DBN framework designed to explicitly capture temporal dependencies and time-varying parameters within cognitive systems. The core innovation lies in constructing a DBN where nodes represent cognitive states, and edges represent probabilistic relationships that change over time. We utilize a time-step indexing system to model the evolution of these relationships, allowing for a more accurate and nuanced depiction of human cognition. The proposed DBN architecture incorporates mechanisms for updating probabilities based on observed evidence, reflecting the adaptive nature of human thinking. This approach offers a powerful tool for understanding and simulating complex cognitive phenomena, particularly those involving rapidly changing information and shifting mental representations. The key advancements include the explicit modeling of temporal dynamics, the incorporation of time-varying parameters, and the design of a DBN structure specifically suited for representing the fluidity of the human mind. We demonstrate, conceptually, the utility of this framework through a simplified example, outlining the structure and key components of a DBN for modeling a basic attention process.

title: Title: Adaptive Complexity Optimization of Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Quantum algorithms, renowned for their potential to solve complex problems beyond the capabilities of classical computers, often face challenges related to computational complexity. This paper introduces a novel approach to address this challenge – Adaptive Complexity Optimization of Quantum Algorithms (ACOA). We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the complexity of quantum algorithms based on the characteristics of the input data. The core mechanism centers around employing a topological quantum algorithm to decompose the algorithm's complexity into modular components, and automatically adjusting these modules based on the input's inherent structure. This adaptive approach aims to improve efficiency and scalability by effectively modeling complex data. The paper details the design of the OACO algorithm, its implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling specific problem instances. We highlight the advantages of this method over traditional complexity optimization techniques, emphasizing its dynamic adaptability and potential for enhanced performance.

title: Towards Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Medical Diagnostic Assistance Systems
abstract: This paper presents a framework for developing explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) based medical diagnostic assistance systems. The core claim is to build systems capable of providing trustworthy diagnostic recommendations alongside transparent explanations of the reasoning process. The proposed mechanism integrates rule-based or case-based reasoning algorithms with deep learning models, leveraging XAI techniques to elucidate the diagnostic logic. This approach addresses the critical need for increased trust and understanding in AI-driven medical diagnoses. The system aims to move beyond "black box" predictions, offering clinicians a clear rationale behind the system's suggestions, thereby facilitating informed decision-making and ultimately improving patient care. The system architecture is described, including the data preprocessing, model training, and explanation generation phases. Furthermore, the paper explores the challenges and future directions in developing robust and reliable XAI-driven diagnostic systems. ---

title: Quantum-Safe Optimization of Asymmetric Encryption Algorithms
abstract: The pursuit of quantum-safe cryptographic algorithms is paramount in the face of emerging quantum computing threats. Existing quantum-safe asymmetric encryption algorithms, such as lattice-based cryptography and code-based cryptography, still present vulnerabilities within their key generation and key exchange processes. This paper investigates these vulnerabilities and proposes an optimization framework leveraging principles from quantum information theory and cryptography to enhance the security of these algorithms. The core claim is that existing quantum-safe asymmetric encryption algorithms have inherent weaknesses in their key generation and key exchange stages. The proposed mechanism utilizes quantum information theory to identify and mitigate these weaknesses, leading to a more secure key generation and key exchange process. Specifically, we explore the application of quantum key distribution (QKD) principles within the asymmetric encryption workflow, coupled with optimized parameter selection based on post-quantum hardness assumptions. The resulting optimized algorithms demonstrate improved resilience against potential attacks leveraging both classical and future quantum computing capabilities. This work contributes to the ongoing effort to develop truly quantum-safe cryptographic solutions.

title: Core Claim: Exploring adaptive topology expansion for quantum computing, leveraging dynamic structural parameter adjustments to achieve quantum computation expansion and complexity.
abstract: Quantum computing offers a paradigm shift in computation, promising unprecedented computational power and solutions to complex problems currently intractable for classical computers. However, current quantum computing architectures are limited by the inherent fragility of qubit states and the difficulty of scaling up quantum systems. This paper investigates adaptive topology expansion, a novel approach to quantum computing that dynamically adjusts the topology of quantum systems to enhance their computational complexity and resilience. We propose a framework based on a system of adjustable parameters that governs the evolution of the quantum state. This system allows for a continuous exploration of quantum states, enabling the efficient mapping of complex problems onto quantum hardware. The core mechanism involves a self-organizing process driven by the interplay of these parameters, creating a robust and adaptable quantum system. Our investigation demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach in achieving significant improvements in quantum entanglement and state fidelity compared to traditional methods. This work presents a fundamental foundation for future advancements in quantum computing, highlighting the potential for dynamically sculpted quantum systems. The significance of this research lies in its ability to overcome limitations inherent in current quantum computing designs, paving the way for more versatile and powerful quantum algorithms.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Domain Adaptation with Disentangled Latent Spaces
abstract: Domain adaptation is a crucial challenge in machine learning, particularly when training models on labeled source data and deploying them on unlabeled target data with differing distributions. Traditional domain adaptation methods often face difficulties in preserving the original source data distribution, leading to reduced accuracy on the target domain. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) with disentangled latent spaces to address this issue. The core idea is to learn domain-invariant representations by decoupling the latent space into independent factors. This allows the generator to reconstruct both source and target data effectively while minimizing domain-specific information. We define the problem as: Let $(s_1, s_2, ..., s_K)$ denote the source data and $(t_1, t_2, ..., t_K)$ denote the target data, where K is the dimensionality of the data. The goal is to learn a mapping $f: \mathbb{R}^K \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^N$ such that $f(z)$ generates data similar to both source and target distributions, where $z$ is a latent vector. The proposed method utilizes a GAN architecture consisting of a Generator and a Discriminator. The Generator learns to map the latent space to both source and target domains, while the Discriminator attempts to distinguish between the generated data and real data from each domain. The disentangled latent space is enforced through a regularization term that encourages independence between the latent factors. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in achieving higher accuracy and better fidelity preservation compared to standard domain adaptation techniques.

title: ##基于量子纠缠的分布式推理引擎
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed reasoning engine leveraging quantum entanglement to overcome the limitations of traditional distributed computing architectures. The core claim is that by exploiting quantum entanglement, we can achieve parallel reasoning between distant nodes without relying on conventional communication channels, thereby significantly enhancing the efficiency of complex computations. The proposed mechanism involves constructing a distributed system composed of multiple quantum processors, each executing a portion of the reasoning task. These processors are interconnected through quantum entanglement, enabling instantaneous information sharing and synchronization, irrespective of the physical distance. This approach directly utilizes the fundamental property of quantum mechanics – quantum entanglement – to avoid communication latency bottlenecks, potentially leading to exponential improvements in computational speed. We present a theoretical framework outlining the architecture and operation of this system, focusing on the key mathematical aspects involved in entanglement management, quantum state synchronization, and reasoning algorithm implementation. The system's performance is analyzed, demonstrating its potential advantages over classical distributed reasoning approaches. ---

title: Quantum State Superposition Distributed Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithm optimization leveraging the principles of quantum state superposition within a distributed computing framework. The core idea centers around decomposing complex optimization problems into a series of smaller, interconnected sub-problems, each represented by a specific quantum state superposition. Quantum entanglement and interference are then strategically employed to facilitate rapid exploration of the global optimization landscape. Unlike traditional optimization methods, this approach aims to harness the inherent parallelism and potential speedup offered by quantum mechanics. The theoretical framework outlines the key mathematical components, including the representation of quantum states, the design of entanglement protocols, and the analysis of interference effects. The paper demonstrates the potential for improved efficiency and accuracy in optimization tasks, particularly those exhibiting high dimensionality or complex dependencies. Further research will focus on developing practical implementations and exploring the scalability of this methodology.

title: Dynamic Semantic Drift Detection and Correction System (DSDCS)
abstract: Modern software systems are increasingly susceptible to semantic drift, a phenomenon characterized by changes in their behavior and functionality due to continuous deployment, evolving user behavior, and shifting external data sources. This drift significantly degrades system quality and user experience. The Dynamic Semantic Drift Detection and Correction System (DSDCS) addresses this challenge with an innovative approach based on continuous learning and adaptive correction. DSDCS employs an Evolutionary Neural Network (ENN) to monitor system behavior in real-time, predict future behavior, and trigger targeted, reversible adjustments when significant deviations are detected. The ENN learns and optimizes correction strategies based on the observed outcomes, creating a closed-loop system for maintaining system semantic health. This system offers a proactive, self-adaptive, and reversible mechanism for semantic drift correction, contrasting with traditional static or manually-driven methods. The core contribution lies in the tightly integrated detection and correction mechanisms, forming a dynamic system capable of responding effectively to evolving system behavior.

title: Explainable Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models Using Evidence-Grounded Verification
abstract: This paper presents Evidence-Grounded Verification (EGV), a modular framework for explainable hallucination detection in large language models. EGV decomposes model outputs into atomic claims, retrieves independent evidence, performs fine-grained four-way verification (Supported, Partially Supported, Contradicted, Unverifiable), and generates template-constrained explanations that are causally linked to the underlying evidence. Unlike most existing detectors that output only a scalar score or binary label, EGV treats explainability as a core architectural requirement. The framework is designed to run on consumer hardware using freely available models. A pilot study on 300 items (600 claims) from the HaluEval QA benchmark (using oracle evidence) compares three verification backends. Results show that a hybrid decision rule combining an off-the-shelf NLI model with simple lexical and length-based features substantially outperforms pure NLI (F1 rises from 3.5% to 65.6%), while a counterfactual evidence-swap test achieves a faithfulness score of 78.0%. The paper provides a full evaluation protocol, an honest analysis of limitations, and clear directions for future validation. This is a Methodology / Framework paper intended as a practical starting point for research on transparent, evidence-grounded hallucination detection.

title: When Knowledge Graph Relationships Still Matter
abstract: Modern language models increasingly recover signals of relatedness from text alone. They can support related-item ranking, entity clustering, and recommendation-style workflows without a separately modeled graph. For the knowledge graph community, this creates a timely and practical question: when do explicit graph relationships still add value beyond what strong text embeddings already capture? This paper approaches that question carefully. It does not treat knowledge graphs as globally replaceable. Many KG roles — including semantic integration, provenance, governance, validation, querying, and domain modeling — remain distinct from embedding-based retrieval. Instead, we focus on a narrower class of use cases where relationship value is representational: recommendation, discovery, similarity search, related-item ranking, and relation recovery. In these settings, the question becomes measurable: do explicit relationships add recoverable signal beyond node text? We introduce a relation-dependent diagnostic framework for measuring this boundary. We call the underlying phenomenon language-model encroachment: the growing ability of text-based representations to approximate relational signal traditionally supplied by explicit graph structure. Using an OpenAlex-derived scientific KG case study, we repeat the diagnostic across relation types, dataset slices, publication years, and text encoders. In each setting, text-derived and graph-derived representations are evaluated on the same held-out relationship recovery task. The results show that the graph–text boundary is not fixed. Some relation types are largely recoverable from text for this task. Others retain distinctive graph-derived signal. The contribution is a practical diagnostic for KG engineering: if a relationship type adds signal beyond text, it may justify graph-engineering effort; if it does not add measurable signal, a text-first system may be sufficient for that task. This does not mean a KG is unnecessary overall, because many KG roles remain justified independently of embedding performance.

abstract: Results for counterfactual image generation for the CRC-VAL-HE-7K dataset. Changes reflect what the model requires to flip the prediction, with increasing manipulation amplitude shown above each image. Horizontal bars show the percentage of image pairs in which at least one of four raters (three board-certified pathologists and one pathology trainee) identified each morphologic feature as present in the original (dark gray) or counterfactual (light gray) image. Right, Mean pairwise inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ) per feature, computed across all pairs and both directions combined. D, Counterfactuals of a healthy mucosa tile shifted toward dysplastic epithelium. Below, Pixel-level difference maps (darker regions indicate greater changes), showing the most change in gland regions, and SSIM values, which quantify the similarity between the original and manipulated tiles. Bottom, Segmented and classified nuclei: pink (epithelial), orange (connective tissue), blue (plasma), deep purple (lymphocytes), aqua (neutrophils), and green (eosinophils). E, Tile-level differences in cell type fractions between (left) real NORM tiles (n = 741) and synthetic (counterfactual images generated from TUM tiles, n = 1,233; full statistical details are provided in Supplementary Table S4). Right, Tile-level differences in cell-type fractions between real TUM tiles (n = 1,233) and synthetic (counterfactual images generated from NORM tiles, n = 741).

title: DeepAffinity: Long-Term Aspect Preference Prediction in eCommerce using Small Language Models
abstract: We explore predicting eCommerce user preferences for product aspects such as brand, size, and color - a task we define as Aspect Affinity. Solving this task improves customer understanding and enables fine-grained personalization in recommendation, search, and marketing. We frame Aspect Affinity as a temporal prediction task: forecasting a users future aspect choices from their time-ordered interaction history, capturing long-term preferences that evolve beyond the current session. To this end, we propose DeepAffinity, which leverages Small Language Models (SLMs) with structured prompts and specialized prediction heads fine-tuned for this task. We show DeepAffinity outperforms standard generative fine-tuning methods, while general-purpose open-source LLMs perform poorly without task-specific tuning, highlighting their limits in modeling nuanced behavior. Finally, DeepAffinity enhances recommendation quality on a large-scale multinational eCommerce platform.

title: A simple derivation of the Kalman filter
abstract: In this lecture note, we present a concise and self-contained derivation of the discrete-time Kalman filter equations that requires only a basic understanding of least squares estimation. The treatment is designed to minimize mathematical overhead while preserving both rigor and generality.

title: SpeakPay: Domain-Adaptive LoRA Fine-Tuning of Whisper for Low-Resource Nepali Financial Speech Recognition
abstract: Mobile payment applications in Nepal are graphically mediated and largely inaccessible to visually impaired users. This paper presents SpeakPay, a voice-first digital wallet, and documents the central technical contribution: a controlled study of domain adaptation for low-resource financial speech recognition. We introduce NepFinSpeech-403, a 403-utterance dataset of Nepali financial voice commands (send, load, and balance operations spanning 237 unique numerals), and fine-tune Whisper large-v2 with LoRA. On the held-out test set, the domain-adapted model reduces Word Error Rate from 129.95% (zero-shot baseline) to 42.58% --- a 67.2% relative reduction --- and improves Devanagari numeral recognition accuracy from 0.0% to 73.9%. We find that word-level metrics understate the practical task-level impact: domain adaptation improves the Transaction Success Rate from 1.67% to 33.33%, a roughly 20x gain. The improvement is consistent at the individual-utterance level (sign test, $p < 10^{-17}$) and across all command types. A data efficiency analysis shows that as few as 100 domain-specific utterances are sufficient to halve the zero-shot WER, with performance plateauing around 300 examples. Error analysis reveals systematic numeral confusion patterns (zero insertion/deletion, prefix hallucination) that account for the majority of remaining transaction failures. The trained system is deployed as a publicly accessible voice-first web application. All code, dataset, model weights, and this paper are released at https://github.com/subedibiraj/speakpay.

title: Polish ModernBERT: The Long and Short of Polish Language Understanding
abstract: Encoder-only Transformers remain effective for discriminative and representation-learning tasks, yet Polish encoders still largely rely on BERT/RoBERTa-style architectures. We introduce \textbf{Polish ModernBERT}, a family of four Polish encoders available at Base and Large scales, each with 512-token and 8K context variants. We adapt the ModernBERT pretraining recipe through staged selection experiments and release a long-context benchmark covering legal topic classification, ideological decision-direction prediction, factual-consistency assessment over literary plot summaries, and human-rights violation assessment. Across 30 tasks, Polish ModernBERT achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated Polish encoders, reaching 83.99 and 85.11 for the Base-8K and Large-8K models, respectively. On long-context tasks, the 8K variants improve over matched Polish RoBERTa-8K baselines from 67.47 to 77.15 and from 75.88 to 78.49 at the Base and Large scales, respectively. The Base-8K model achieves this gain with 22\% fewer parameters (149M vs.\ 190M). Efficiency measurements in representative inference setups show lower peak memory usage and latency than matched Polish RoBERTa baselines in both 512-token and 8K settings. Polish ModernBERT-8K-Base additionally achieves the best result on a Polish retrieval benchmark among the evaluated encoders below 300M parameters.

title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
abstract: AI tutors are most useful when they adapt to each student's strengths, weaknesses, and preferred guidance, but evidence about which guidance works for which student is sparse, slow, and costly to collect from real learners. Student simulators can provide this signal as a proxy, yet existing approaches are limited: state-tracking models fit student behavior but struggle to process explanations or corrections, while LLM role-play follows guidance fluently but does not reliably match the competence of the student being imitated. We present StudentSim, a training framework that turns sparse per-student data into individualized simulators through pooled training followed by per-student specialization. The resulting simulators both mirror a student's own responses and update them under tutor guidance. We also introduce StudentSimEval, a standardized protocol covering 60 students across chess, second-language English writing, and mathematics, using public learner datasets with de-identified records shared for research. StudentSimEval measures behavioral fidelity (F), or how well a simulator matches a student's responses, and guidance responsiveness (R), or how readily it updates under tutor guidance, with all methods fit and evaluated on the same records. Across all three domains, StudentSim outperforms GPT-5.4 on both metrics. In chess, StudentSim reaches F=0.51 and R=0.91, compared with 0.23 and 0.72 for GPT-5.4 and 0.45 and 0.27 for Maia2. As a proof of concept, using StudentSim as a reward model for tutor reinforcement learning produces a chess tutor that expert humans rate as more accurate, better-guided, and more personalized than a no-RL baseline and a tutor trained against a GPT-5.4 simulator reward. Code is available at https://github.com/microsoft/StudentSim.
